# Filmed Screen
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/components/filmed-screen

Your scene, filmed off a screen: perspective, depth of field that follows an element you name, LED sub-pixels and per-shot colour grades. Shots glide into each other, focus racks between elements, and the focused element stays sharp.

# Filmed Screen

Your scene, filmed off a screen: perspective, depth of field that follows an element you name, LED sub-pixels and per-shot colour grades. Shots glide into each other, focus racks between elements, and the focused element stays sharp.

**Filmed Screen**

```html filmed-screen.html theme={null}
<!--
  Filmed Screen — films your scene like a camera pointed at a monitor: perspective tilt,
  a gently curved screen, depth of field that follows an element you name, chromatic
  fringing, LED sub-pixels, a vignette, a per-shot colour grade, and shots that glide (or
  orbit) into each other, or cut with a tear.
  The focused element stays sharp, and focus racks smoothly between elements.

  Usage: paste this snippet into your composition and put your scene inside
  .hf-filmed-screen-scene. Then edit the HFFilmedScreen.mount() call at the bottom.

  Requirements:
  - Chrome with HTML-in-Canvas (the HyperFrames renderer has it). Without it the lens
    steps aside and the scene renders unfilmed.
  - Keep the <canvas layoutsubtree> in the HTML. Created from script, the renderer never
    sees it and captures blank frames.
  - .hf-filmed-screen-scene needs an explicit pixel size; inset:0 measures 0×0 inside the canvas.
  - Rendering uses screenshot capture on one worker, so expect slower renders.

  HFFilmedScreen.mount({ canvas, shots, rack, vignette, aberration, led, curve, fadeOut, zIndex })
    → { destroy() }
    canvas  — element, list or selector; the first one not already filmed is used. Pass your
              own document.querySelectorAll(...) so each instance finds its own canvas.
              A <canvas layoutsubtree> films its first child (DOM); any other canvas
              (p5, three.js…) is sampled directly.
    fadeOut — fade to black over the last 0.4 s of the composition (default true)
    zIndex  — z-index of the lens output canvas (default 10)
    rack    — seconds a focus change takes to settle (default 0.3)
    vignette   — edge darkening (default 1.0; 0 turns it off)
    aberration — chromatic fringing, × the base amount (default 2.2)
    led        — LED sub-pixel grid strength (default 0.45)
    curve      — screen curvature (default 0.15; 0 is flat)
    shots   — [{ until, palette, invert, tilt, tiltTo, zoom, blur, center, focus, transition, glide }]
      until    end of the shot, in seconds of this composition's timeline
      palette  5 hex colours, dark → light; null keeps true colour
      invert   true flips brightness, keeping hue (light pages → dark screens)
      tilt     [x, y, roll] radians
      tiltTo   tilt to end the shot on, for an orbit (default: tilt)
      zoom     [from, to] across the shot
      blur     depth-of-field strength (default 0.45; ~1 for a shallow phone look)
      center   [x, y] where the camera points when nothing is in focus
      focus    (t, local) → Element | {x, y, w, h} | array (last one is the focus)
      transition  "glide" (default) eases in from the previous shot; "cut" cuts with a tear
      glide    seconds the glide takes (default 1.2)
-->
<canvas
  class="hf-filmed-screen"
  layoutsubtree
  width="1920"
  height="1080"
  style="position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1920px; height: 1080px"
>
  <div
    class="hf-filmed-screen-scene"
    style="
      position: absolute;
      left: 0;
      top: 0;
      width: 1920px;
      height: 1080px;
      overflow: hidden;
      background: #0b0d12;
    "
  >
    <!-- your scene here -->
  </div>
</canvas>

<script>
  (function () {
    // Inside a sub-composition `window` is a scoping Proxy that hands back functions bound,
    // so identity checks on hooks always fail. Engine hooks go on the real global.
    var G = globalThis;
    if (G.HFFilmedScreen) return;
    var FOCAL = 1.7;

    var FRAG = `#version 300 es
precision highp float;
uniform sampler2D uSrc;
uniform vec2 uRes; uniform float uTime; uniform vec2 uAim; uniform float uZoom; uniform vec3 uRot;
uniform vec2 uFocus; uniform vec4 uFocusRect; uniform float uBlur; uniform vec3 uP[5]; uniform float uTrue;
uniform float uCut; uniform float uOut; uniform float uSeed; uniform float uInv;
uniform float uVig; uniform float uCA; uniform float uLed; uniform float uCurve;
out vec4 outColor;
const float FOCAL = 1.7; const float CELL = 3.0;
const int TAPS = 36; const int GLOW_TAPS = 16;
const vec3 LUMA = vec3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114);
float hash(vec2 p) { return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453); }
vec3 pal(float x) {
  float t = clamp(x, 0.0, 1.0) * 4.0;
  if (t < 1.0) return mix(uP[0], uP[1], t);
  if (t < 2.0) return mix(uP[1], uP[2], t - 1.0);
  if (t < 3.0) return mix(uP[2], uP[3], t - 2.0);
  return mix(uP[3], uP[4], t - 3.0);
}
vec3 screenAt(vec2 q) {
  float inside = step(0.0, q.x) * step(0.0, q.y) * step(q.x, uRes.x) * step(q.y, uRes.y);
  vec3 c = texture(uSrc, q / uRes).rgb;
  c = mix(c, clamp(c + (1.0 - 2.0 * dot(c, LUMA)), 0.0, 1.0), uInv);
  return c * inside;
}
mat3 rotation() {
  float cx = cos(uRot.x); float sx = sin(uRot.x); float cy = cos(uRot.y); float sy = sin(uRot.y);
  float cz = cos(uRot.z); float sz = sin(uRot.z);
  mat3 rx = mat3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0,  0.0, cx, sx,  0.0, -sx, cx);
  mat3 ry = mat3(cy, 0.0, -sy,  0.0, 1.0, 0.0,  sy, 0.0, cy);
  mat3 rz = mat3(cz, sz, 0.0,  -sz, cz, 0.0,  0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  return rz * ry * rx;
}
float wt(float l) { return 1.0 + 7.0 * l * l * l; }
void main() {
  vec2 res = uRes;
  vec2 coord = vec2(gl_FragCoord.x, res.y - gl_FragCoord.y);
  vec2 frameSeed = vec2(uSeed, floor(uTime * 30.0));
  vec2 px = coord;
  if (uCut > 0.0) {
    float band = floor(coord.y / 16.0);
    float n = hash(vec2(band, frameSeed.x * 3.7 + frameSeed.y));
    px.x += step(0.93 - 0.18 * uCut, n) * (hash(vec2(band, frameSeed.y + 9.0)) - 0.5) * 220.0 * uCut;
  }
  vec2 s0 = (px - 0.5 * res) / res.y;
  // Barrel curve, normalised so the frame's corners stay put: the middle swells toward the
  // camera and straight lines bow outward, without the page edge entering the shot.
  vec2 corner = 0.5 * res / res.y;
  vec2 s = s0 * (1.0 + uCurve * dot(s0, s0)) / (1.0 + uCurve * dot(corner, corner));
  vec3 d = vec3(s.x, s.y, FOCAL);
  mat3 R = rotation();
  vec3 eu = R * vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); vec3 ev = R * vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); vec3 nrm = R * vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  vec3 p0 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  float dn = dot(d, nrm);
  if (dn <= 0.0001) { outColor = vec4(vec3(0.0), 1.0); return; }
  vec3 hit3 = d * (dot(p0, nrm) / dn);
  vec2 local = vec2(dot(hit3 - p0, eu), dot(hit3 - p0, ev));
  float K = FOCAL * res.y / uZoom;
  vec2 base = uAim + local * K;
  float z = hit3.z;
  vec2 fl = (uFocus - uAim) / K;
  float zf = (p0 + eu * fl.x + ev * fl.y).z;
  // The focused element stays legible: 1 inside its rect, easing to 0 over ~160 source px.
  vec2 fd = max(abs(base - (uFocusRect.xy + 0.5 * uFocusRect.zw)) - 0.5 * uFocusRect.zw, 0.0);
  float sharp = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 160.0, length(fd));
  float coc = clamp(uBlur * 190.0 * abs(1.0 - zf / z), 0.0, 46.0) * (1.0 - sharp);
  float logPerPx = 1.0 / uZoom * z;
  float rLog = coc * logPerPx;
  // A trace of fringing survives on the focused text (a quarter), enough to read as glass.
  vec2 ca = (1.0 - 0.75 * sharp) * uCA * s * (0.006 + 0.008 * uCut) * (res.y / uZoom);
  float snapAmt = smoothstep(0.5 * CELL, 2.0 * CELL, rLog);
  float spin = hash(coord * 0.37 + frameSeed) * 6.2831;
  vec3 accC = vec3(0.0); float accGl = 0.0; float accRr = 0.0; float accRl = 0.0; float accBb = 0.0; float accBl = 0.0;
  float wG = 0.0; float wR = 0.0; float wB = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < TAPS; i++) {
    float fi = float(i);
    float a = fi * 2.39996323 + spin;
    float r = sqrt((fi + 0.5) / float(TAPS)) * rLog;
    vec2 q = base + vec2(cos(a), sin(a)) * r;
    // Snap to LED cells only where blur hides it; snapping sharp text turns glyphs to blocks.
    vec2 qs = mix(q, (floor(q / CELL) + 0.5) * CELL, snapAmt);
    vec3 c0 = screenAt(qs); vec3 cr = screenAt(qs + ca); vec3 cb = screenAt(qs - ca);
    float l0 = dot(c0, LUMA); float lr = dot(cr, LUMA); float lb = dot(cb, LUMA);
    // Each channel weighted by its own sample, or blurred texture picks up a green cast.
    float w0 = wt(l0); float wr = wt(lr); float wb = wt(lb);
    accC += c0 * w0; accGl += l0 * w0; wG += w0;
    accRr += cr.r * wr; accRl += lr * wr; wR += wr;
    accBb += cb.b * wb; accBl += lb * wb; wB += wb;
  }
  accC /= wG; accGl /= wG; accRr /= wR; accRl /= wR; accBb /= wB; accBl /= wB;
  // uTrue blends graded and true colour, so a glide between shots can cross-fade the grade.
  vec3 graded = vec3(pal(accRl).r, pal(accGl).g, pal(accBl).b);
  float red = clamp((accC.r - max(accC.g, accC.b)) * 1.4, 0.0, 1.0);
  graded = mix(graded, vec3(1.0, 0.13, 0.10), red);
  vec3 col = mix(graded, vec3(accRr, accC.g, accBb), uTrue);
  float glowR = 26.0 * logPerPx + rLog * 0.6;
  float glow = 0.0; vec3 glowC = vec3(0.0);
  for (int j = 0; j < GLOW_TAPS; j++) {
    float fj = float(j);
    float a = fj * 2.39996323 + spin * 0.5;
    float r = sqrt((fj + 0.5) / float(GLOW_TAPS)) * glowR;
    vec3 g = screenAt(base + vec2(cos(a), sin(a)) * r);
    float l = dot(g, LUMA);
    glow += l * l; glowC += g * l;
  }
  glow /= float(GLOW_TAPS); glowC /= float(GLOW_TAPS);
  vec3 glowTint = mix(pal(min(1.0, glow * 1.6)) * glow, glowC, uTrue);
  col += glowTint * 0.6 * (1.0 - 0.6 * sharp);
  vec2 cu = fract(base / CELL) - 0.5;
  vec3 sub = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(6.2831853 * (vec3(cu.x + 0.5) - vec3(0.1667, 0.5, 0.8333)));
  float rowm = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.28, 0.5, abs(cu.y));
  float colm = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.36, 0.5, abs(cu.x));
  vec3 led = rowm * colm * (0.4 + 1.0 * sub);
  // The grid only shows once a cell spans ~4 output px; finer, it aliases into moiré.
  float ledAmt = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.8, 3.5, rLog / CELL)) * smoothstep(4.0, 6.5, CELL / logPerPx);
  col *= mix(vec3(1.0), led * 1.3, ledAmt * uLed * (1.0 - 0.7 * sharp));
  col = col * (1.0 + uCut * 1.1) + uCut * 0.06;
  vec2 v = s0 * vec2(0.85, 1.15);
  col *= max(0.0, 1.0 - uVig * dot(v, v));
  col *= 1.0 - (0.035 - 0.035 * sin(coord.y * 0.9 - uTime * 55.0));
  col += (hash(coord + frameSeed * 1.31) - 0.5) * 0.06;
  col *= 1.0 - uOut;
  outColor = vec4(clamp(col, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0);
}`;
    var VERT = "#version 300 es\nin vec2 a;\nvoid main(){ gl_Position = vec4(a, 0.0, 1.0); }";

    function clamp(x, a, b) {
      return Math.min(b, Math.max(a, x));
    }
    function hex(h) {
      var n = parseInt(h.slice(1), 16);
      return [((n >> 16) & 255) / 255, ((n >> 8) & 255) / 255, (n & 255) / 255];
    }

    // One owner of the engine's seek + composite hooks, fanning out to every lens on the page.
    var lenses = [];
    var lastSeekT = 0,
      seq = 0,
      resolvedSeq = -1,
      myPrepare = null,
      myResolve = null,
      preparing = false,
      resolving = false;
    function live() {
      lenses = lenses.filter(function (l) {
        return l.src.isConnected !== false;
      });
      return lenses;
    }
    // Co-owners of the composite slot (core's data-vfx-chain among them) re-wrap it on every
    // seek and read their prior when called, so a stale wrapper of ours is re-entered through
    // them. Each wrapper keeps its own prior, and a re-entered one returns at once, so the
    // chain stays a constant depth. In the engine's order (vfx arms inside the seek, this hook
    // after it returns) every owner runs exactly once per frame.
    function arm() {
      if (!live().length) return;
      if (G.__hf_page_composite_prepare !== myPrepare) {
        var priorPrepare =
          typeof G.__hf_page_composite_prepare === "function"
            ? G.__hf_page_composite_prepare
            : null;
        myPrepare = async function () {
          if (preparing) return false;
          preparing = true;
          try {
            var p = priorPrepare ? await priorPrepare() : false;
            live().forEach(function (l) {
              l.prepare();
            });
            return p;
          } finally {
            preparing = false;
          }
        };
        G.__hf_page_composite_prepare = myPrepare;
      }
      if (G.__hf_page_composite_resolve !== myResolve) {
        var priorResolve =
          typeof G.__hf_page_composite_resolve === "function"
            ? G.__hf_page_composite_resolve
            : null;
        myResolve = function () {
          if (resolving) return false;
          resolving = true;
          try {
            var p = priorResolve ? priorResolve() : false;
            var ok = false;
            live().forEach(function (l) {
              ok = l.draw() || ok;
            });
            resolvedSeq = seq;
            G.__hf_page_composite_pending = false;
            return ok || p;
          } finally {
            resolving = false;
          }
        };
        G.__hf_page_composite_resolve = myResolve;
      }
      G.__hf_page_composite_pending = true;
    }
    // Preview and snapshot never call the resolver: wait for a paint, then draw.
    function previewFrame(my) {
      setTimeout(function () {
        if (my !== seq || resolvedSeq >= my) return;
        live().forEach(function (l) {
          l.prepare();
          l.afterPaint(function () {
            if (my === seq && resolvedSeq < my) l.draw();
          });
        });
      }, 0);
    }
    function onSeek(t) {
      lastSeekT = Number(t) || 0;
      var my = ++seq;
      arm();
      previewFrame(my);
    }
    // Renders seek through __hf.seek; snapshot and Studio through __player.renderSeek / seek.
    // __hf.seek is an accessor that wraps whatever is assigned, so a marker on the function
    // never survives: remember what is hooked instead, or every poll wraps it again.
    var hooked = {};
    function hook(obj, key) {
      if (hooked[obj + "." + key]) return true;
      var o = G[obj];
      if (!o || typeof o[key] !== "function") return false;
      var orig = o[key];
      o[key] = function () {
        var r = orig.apply(this, arguments);
        onSeek(arguments[0]);
        return r;
      };
      hooked[obj + "." + key] = true;
      return true;
    }
    (function poll(n) {
      var a = hook("__hf", "seek"),
        b = hook("__player", "renderSeek"),
        c = hook("__player", "seek");
      if (!(a && b && c) && n < 500)
        setTimeout(function () {
          poll(n + 1);
        }, 20);
    })(0);

    var MOUNTED = "data-filmed-screen-mounted";
    function mount(opts) {
      // The library initialises once per page, so its own `document` may be another
      // sub-composition's scope. The snippet passes its caller-scoped query result; the first
      // canvas not already filmed is this instance's.
      var c = opts.canvas;
      var candidates =
        typeof c === "string"
          ? Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(c)).concat(
              Array.from(G.document.querySelectorAll(c)),
            )
          : c && typeof c.getContext !== "function"
            ? Array.from(c)
            : [c];
      var src = candidates.filter(function (el) {
        return el && !el.hasAttribute(MOUNTED);
      })[0];
      if (!src) throw new Error("[filmed-screen] no unmounted canvas matches " + c);
      src.setAttribute(MOUNTED, "");
      var comp = src.closest("[data-composition-id]");
      var compId = comp && comp.getAttribute("data-composition-id");
      var DUR = Number(comp && comp.getAttribute("data-duration")) || Infinity;
      var shots = opts.shots;
      var W = src.width,
        H = src.height;
      var screenEl = src.hasAttribute("layoutsubtree") ? src.firstElementChild : null;
      var srcCtx = screenEl ? src.getContext("2d") : null;

      // No HTML-in-Canvas or no WebGL2: put the scene back in the page and step aside.
      function stepAside(why) {
        if (screenEl) {
          src.parentNode.insertBefore(screenEl, src);
          src.remove();
        }
        console.warn(
          "[filmed-screen] " + why + " unavailable; rendering the scene without the lens",
        );
        return { destroy: function () {} };
      }
      if (screenEl && !(srcCtx && srcCtx.drawElementImage)) return stepAside("HTML-in-Canvas");

      // The filmed scene sits under the lens on purpose. The layout audit reads the flag on each
      // text element, not its ancestors.
      // ponytail: elements added after mount miss it; the real fix is the audit skipping
      // canvas[layoutsubtree] descendants, which are never painted.
      if (screenEl)
        [screenEl].concat(Array.from(screenEl.querySelectorAll("*"))).forEach(function (el) {
          el.setAttribute("data-layout-allow-occlusion", "");
        });

      var out = document.createElement("canvas");
      out.width = W;
      out.height = H;
      out.className = "hf-filmed-screen-out";
      out.style.cssText =
        "position:absolute;left:" +
        src.offsetLeft +
        "px;top:" +
        src.offsetTop +
        "px;width:" +
        src.offsetWidth +
        "px;height:" +
        src.offsetHeight +
        "px;z-index:" +
        (opts.zIndex || 10) +
        ";pointer-events:none";
      src.parentNode.insertBefore(out, src.nextSibling);

      var gl = out.getContext("webgl2", { preserveDrawingBuffer: true, antialias: false });
      if (!gl) {
        out.remove();
        return stepAside("WebGL2");
      }
      function sh(type, s) {
        var x = gl.createShader(type);
        gl.shaderSource(x, s);
        gl.compileShader(x);
        if (!gl.getShaderParameter(x, gl.COMPILE_STATUS))
          throw new Error("[filmed-screen] " + gl.getShaderInfoLog(x));
        return x;
      }
      var prog = gl.createProgram();
      gl.attachShader(prog, sh(gl.VERTEX_SHADER, VERT));
      gl.attachShader(prog, sh(gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER, FRAG));
      gl.linkProgram(prog);
      gl.useProgram(prog);
      gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, gl.createBuffer());
      gl.bufferData(
        gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,
        new Float32Array([-1, -1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1, 1]),
        gl.STATIC_DRAW,
      );
      var aLoc = gl.getAttribLocation(prog, "a");
      gl.enableVertexAttribArray(aLoc);
      gl.vertexAttribPointer(aLoc, 2, gl.FLOAT, false, 0, 0);
      var loc = {};
      "uSrc uRes uTime uAim uZoom uRot uFocus uFocusRect uBlur uP uTrue uCut uOut uSeed uInv uVig uCA uLed uCurve"
        .split(" ")
        .forEach(function (n) {
          loc[n] = gl.getUniformLocation(prog, n);
        });
      var tex = gl.createTexture();
      gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D, tex);
      [gl.TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, gl.TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER].forEach(function (p) {
        gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D, p, gl.LINEAR);
      });
      [gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_S, gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_T].forEach(function (p) {
        gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D, p, gl.CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
      });
      gl.viewport(0, 0, W, H);

      // Seconds on this composition's own timeline, so shots work inside sub-compositions.
      function now() {
        var tl =
          compId &&
          ((window.__timelines && window.__timelines[compId]) ||
            (G.__timelines && G.__timelines[compId]));
        return tl && typeof tl.time === "function" ? tl.time() : lastSeekT;
      }
      function shotAt(t) {
        var start = 0;
        for (var i = 0; i < shots.length; i++) {
          if (t < shots[i].until || i === shots.length - 1)
            return { i: i, shot: shots[i], local: t - start, start: start };
          start = shots[i].until;
        }
      }
      function rectOf(target) {
        if (!target) return null;
        if (!(target instanceof Element)) return target;
        if (
          target.checkVisibility &&
          !target.checkVisibility({ opacityProperty: true, visibilityProperty: true })
        )
          return null;
        var r = target.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (r.width < 2 || r.height < 2) return null;
        var o = (screenEl || src).getBoundingClientRect();
        return {
          x: ((r.left - o.left) * W) / o.width,
          y: ((r.top - o.top) * H) / o.height,
          w: (r.width * W) / o.width,
          h: (r.height * H) / o.height,
        };
      }
      function smoother(x) {
        x = clamp(x, 0, 1);
        return x * x * x * (x * (x * 6 - 15) + 10);
      }
      function lerp(a, b, k) {
        return a + (b - a) * k;
      }
      function lerpArr(a, b, k) {
        return a.map(function (v, i) {
          return lerp(v, b[i], k);
        });
      }
      // One shot's camera at `local` seconds into it. Everything here is a pure function of time.
      function shotCam(i, local) {
        var sh = shots[i],
          start = i > 0 ? shots[i - 1].until : 0,
          len = Math.max(0.001, sh.until - start);
        var sway = Math.sin(i * 1.7 + local * 0.9) * 0.012;
        var tilt = sh.tilt || [0.1, -0.15, 0.02],
          tiltTo = sh.tiltTo || tilt,
          zoom = sh.zoom || [1.1, 1.3];
        return {
          center: sh.center || [W / 2, H / 2],
          // An orbit: the tilt eases from `tilt` to `tiltTo` across the shot.
          rot: [0, 1, 2].map(function (k) {
            return lerp(tilt[k], tiltTo[k], smoother(local / len)) + sway * [1, -0.7, 0.4][k];
          }),
          zoom: lerp(zoom[0], zoom[1], smoother(local / len)),
          blur: sh.blur == null ? 0.45 : sh.blur,
          pal: sh.palette ? [].concat.apply([], sh.palette.map(hex)) : null,
          trueAmt: sh.palette ? 0 : 1,
          inv: sh.invert ? 1 : 0,
        };
      }
      // Shots glide into each other by default: camera, grade and colour mode ease over
      // `glide` seconds. `transition: "cut"` keeps the hard cut and its tear.
      function camAt(t) {
        var s = shotAt(t),
          cam = shotCam(s.i, s.local),
          sh = s.shot;
        cam.cut = 0;
        if (s.i > 0 && sh.transition === "cut") {
          cam.cut = Math.max(0, 1 - s.local * 15);
        } else if (s.i > 0) {
          var glide = sh.glide == null ? 1.2 : sh.glide;
          if (s.local < glide) {
            var prevLen = shots[s.i - 1].until - (s.i > 1 ? shots[s.i - 2].until : 0);
            var p = shotCam(s.i - 1, prevLen + s.local),
              k = smoother(s.local / glide);
            if (!p.pal) p.pal = cam.pal;
            if (!cam.pal) cam.pal = p.pal;
            ["zoom", "blur", "trueAmt", "inv"].forEach(function (key) {
              cam[key] = lerp(p[key], cam[key], k);
            });
            cam.center = lerpArr(p.center, cam.center, k);
            cam.rot = lerpArr(p.rot, cam.rot, k);
            if (cam.pal) cam.pal = lerpArr(p.pal, cam.pal, k);
          }
        }
        return { s: s, cam: cam };
      }
      function focusRectAt(t, fallback) {
        var s = shotAt(Math.max(0, t)),
          sh = s.shot;
        var picked = sh.focus ? sh.focus(Math.max(0, t), s.local) : null;
        var rects = []
          .concat(picked || [])
          .map(rectOf)
          .filter(Boolean);
        var f = rects[rects.length - 1];
        return f ? [f.x - 8, f.y - 6, f.w + 16, f.h + 12] : fallback;
      }
      // Focus racks instead of snapping: over the last `rack` seconds, take the target each shot
      // named at that moment, measure where it sits in the DOM now, and Hann-average the boxes.
      // A new target eases in on an S-curve, and with no state kept, any seek order gives the
      // same frame.
      var RACK_TAPS = 12;
      var fs = null,
        awaitingPaint = false;
      function prepare() {
        var t = now(),
          at = camAt(t),
          cam = at.cam;
        var rack = opts.rack == null ? 0.3 : opts.rack;
        var still = [cam.center[0], cam.center[1], 0, 0];
        var rect = [0, 0, 0, 0],
          wsum = 0;
        for (var i = 0; i < RACK_TAPS; i++) {
          var w = 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos((2 * Math.PI * (i + 0.5)) / RACK_TAPS);
          var r = focusRectAt(t - (rack * i) / (RACK_TAPS - 1), still);
          for (var j = 0; j < 4; j++) rect[j] += r[j] * w;
          wsum += w;
        }
        rect = rect.map(function (v) {
          return v / wsum;
        });
        var focus = [rect[0] + rect[2] / 2, rect[1] + rect[3] / 2];
        fs = {
          t: t,
          cam: cam,
          rect: rect,
          focus: focus,
          aim: [focus[0] * 0.65 + cam.center[0] * 0.35, focus[1] * 0.65 + cam.center[1] * 0.35],
          out: opts.fadeOut === false || !isFinite(DUR) ? 0 : clamp((t - (DUR - 0.4)) / 0.4, 0, 1),
          seed: at.s.i * 31 + Math.floor(at.s.local * 30),
        };
      }
      function draw() {
        // A composition that isn't on screen yet (or any more) has no paint record to capture.
        if (
          src.checkVisibility &&
          !src.checkVisibility({ opacityProperty: true, visibilityProperty: true })
        )
          return false;
        if (!fs) prepare();
        if (screenEl) {
          try {
            srcCtx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
            srcCtx.drawElementImage(screenEl, 0, 0);
          } catch (e) {
            // Before the scene's first paint there is nothing to capture yet. That is a wait,
            // not a failure: ask for a paint and draw again when it lands.
            if (/paint record/i.test(e.message)) {
              if (!awaitingPaint) {
                awaitingPaint = true;
                src.addEventListener(
                  "paint",
                  function () {
                    awaitingPaint = false;
                    draw();
                  },
                  { once: true },
                );
                try {
                  if (src.requestPaint) src.requestPaint();
                } catch (_) {}
              }
              return false;
            }
            console.error("[filmed-screen] capture failed: " + e.message);
            return false;
          }
        }
        var cam = fs.cam;
        gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D, tex);
        gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D, 0, gl.RGBA, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, src);
        gl.uniform1i(loc.uSrc, 0);
        gl.uniform2f(loc.uRes, W, H);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uTime, fs.t);
        gl.uniform2f(loc.uAim, fs.aim[0], fs.aim[1]);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uZoom, cam.zoom);
        gl.uniform3f(loc.uRot, cam.rot[0], cam.rot[1], cam.rot[2]);
        gl.uniform2f(loc.uFocus, fs.focus[0], fs.focus[1]);
        gl.uniform4f(loc.uFocusRect, fs.rect[0], fs.rect[1], fs.rect[2], fs.rect[3]);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uBlur, cam.blur);
        gl.uniform3fv(loc.uP, cam.pal || new Array(15).fill(0));
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uTrue, cam.trueAmt);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uCut, cam.cut);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uOut, fs.out);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uSeed, fs.seed);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uInv, cam.inv);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uVig, opts.vignette == null ? 1.0 : opts.vignette);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uCA, opts.aberration == null ? 2.2 : opts.aberration);
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uLed, opts.led == null ? 0.45 : opts.led);
        // A negative curve would sample outside the frame and fold over.
        gl.uniform1f(loc.uCurve, Math.max(0, opts.curve == null ? 0.15 : opts.curve));
        gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4);
        fs = null;
        return true;
      }
      function afterPaint(go) {
        if (!screenEl) return go();
        var done = false;
        function once() {
          if (!done) {
            done = true;
            go();
          }
        }
        src.addEventListener("paint", once, { once: true });
        try {
          if (src.requestPaint) src.requestPaint();
        } catch (e) {}
        setTimeout(once, 250);
      }
      var lens = { src: src, prepare: prepare, draw: draw, afterPaint: afterPaint };
      lenses.push(lens);
      // A lens whose canvas leaves the page is dropped on the next frame; destroy() also frees
      // its GL context. The seek hooks stay: they are shared by every lens on the page.
      return {
        destroy: function () {
          lenses = lenses.filter(function (l) {
            return l !== lens;
          });
          var lose = gl.getExtension("WEBGL_lose_context");
          if (lose) lose.loseContext();
          out.remove();
          src.removeAttribute(MOUNTED);
        },
      };
    }

    G.HFFilmedScreen = { mount: mount };
  })();
</script>

<script>
  // An orbit across two shots: a wide establishing shot, then a close-up that follows the
  // headline and the paragraph while the camera swings to the same angle on the other side.
  HFFilmedScreen.mount({
    canvas: document.querySelectorAll(".hf-filmed-screen"),
    shots: [
      {
        until: 2.5,
        palette: null,
        tilt: [0.06, 0.24, -0.02],
        tiltTo: [0.08, 0.14, -0.012],
        zoom: [1.28, 1.38],
        focus: function () {
          return document.querySelector(".hf-filmed-screen-scene h1");
        },
      },
      {
        until: 6,
        palette: null,
        tilt: [0.1, 0.14, -0.012],
        tiltTo: [0.06, -0.24, 0.02],
        zoom: [2.0, 2.4],
        focus: function () {
          return document.querySelector(".hf-filmed-screen-scene p");
        },
      },
    ],
  });
</script>
```

# Focus Blur Resolve
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/components/focus-blur-resolve

A premium focus pull from heavy blur to crisp text, then a soft blur-out exit.

# Focus Blur Resolve

A premium focus pull from heavy blur to crisp text, then a soft blur-out exit.

**Focus Blur Resolve**

```html focus-blur-resolve.html theme={null}
<!--
  Focus Blur Resolve - typography primitive for HyperFrames.

  Paste the markup and CSS into a composition. Drive the timeline integration
  from a paused GSAP timeline so renders remain deterministic.

  Variables. The script reads each one, falls back to the declared default on
  anything missing or unrecognised, and writes the result as a custom property
  the CSS consumes. The timeline recipe below is untouched by them: it keeps
  driving one scale and one blur, and these decide how big the words are, what
  colour they resolve to, and how deep the blur they resolve from goes.

    - tone (ink | paper | accent, default ink): word colour. ink is near-black
      for light frames, paper near-white for dark ones, accent rides --brand.
    - size (compact | standard | display, default standard): type size, 40px,
      56px or 84px.
    - blur (soft | standard | heavy, default standard): scales the blur radius,
      so the pull starts as a light haze or a full smear over the same run.

  On every default the result is identical to the original: near-black 56px
  words resolving out of a 16px blur.
-->

<div
  class="hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve"
  data-composition-variables='[
    { "id": "tone", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Tone", "description": "Word colour: ink for light frames, paper for dark ones, accent rides --brand.", "default": "ink", "options": [{ "value": "ink", "label": "Ink" }, { "value": "paper", "label": "Paper" }, { "value": "accent", "label": "Accent" }] },
    { "id": "size", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Size", "description": "Type size of the words, from a caption-scale line to a full display card.", "default": "standard", "options": [{ "value": "compact", "label": "Compact" }, { "value": "standard", "label": "Standard" }, { "value": "display", "label": "Display" }] },
    { "id": "blur", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Blur", "description": "Scales the blur radius the timeline drives, so the focus pull starts as a light haze or a full smear.", "default": "standard", "options": [{ "value": "soft", "label": "Soft" }, { "value": "standard", "label": "Standard" }, { "value": "heavy", "label": "Heavy" }] }
  ]'
>
  <span>Crystal</span><span>clear</span>
</div>

<style>
  .hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve {
    color: var(--hf-word-color, #18181b);
    font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif;
    font-weight: 900;
    letter-spacing: -0.04em;
  }
  .hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve {
    display: inline-flex;
    gap: 12px;
    font-size: var(--hf-word-size, 56px);
    line-height: 1;
  }
  .hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve span {
    display: inline-block;
    transform: translate(var(--hf-word-x, 0px), var(--hf-word-y, 0px))
      scale(var(--hf-word-scale, 1));
    filter: blur(calc(var(--hf-word-blur, 0px) * var(--hf-word-blur-scale, 1)));
    will-change: transform, filter, opacity;
  }
</style>

<script>
  (function () {
    "use strict";

    var vars =
      window.__hyperframes && window.__hyperframes.getVariables
        ? window.__hyperframes.getVariables()
        : {};

    // Unrecognised overrides return to their declared defaults.
    function pick(table, value, fallback) {
      return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(table, value) ? value : fallback;
    }

    var tones = { ink: "#18181b", paper: "#fafafa", accent: "var(--brand, #34d399)" };
    var sizes = { compact: "40px", standard: "56px", display: "84px" };
    var blurScales = { soft: 0.45, standard: 1, heavy: 2.2 };

    var tone = tones[pick(tones, vars.tone, "ink")];
    var size = sizes[pick(sizes, vars.size, "standard")];
    var blurScale = blurScales[pick(blurScales, vars.blur, "standard")];

    var roots = document.querySelectorAll(".hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve");
    for (var i = 0; i < roots.length; i += 1) {
      roots[i].style.setProperty("--hf-word-color", tone);
      roots[i].style.setProperty("--hf-word-size", size);
      roots[i].style.setProperty("--hf-word-blur-scale", String(blurScale));
    }
  })();
</script>

<!--
  Timeline integration:
  tl.fromTo('.hf-catalog-focus-blur-resolve span', { opacity: 0, '--hf-word-scale': 1.08, '--hf-word-blur': '16px' }, { opacity: 1, '--hf-word-scale': 1, '--hf-word-blur': '0px', duration: 0.52, stagger: 0.05, ease: 'power3.out' }, startTime);
-->
```

# Focus Rack
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/components/focus-rack

Focus shifts once between two cards at different apparent depths through synchronized blur, dimming, scale, and parallax.

# Focus Rack

Focus shifts once between two cards at different apparent depths through synchronized blur, dimming, scale, and parallax.

**Focus Rack**

```html focus-rack.html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<!--
  focus-rack: HyperFrames video primitive (camera / holdable / emphasize)

  Concept: two cards sit at different apparent depths. Card A begins sharp
  and near while card B is blurred and dim. Focus moves to card B exactly
  once, with blur, scale, and parallax changing together over 0.7 seconds.

  Variables:
    - label_a (string, default "Draft"): foreground card label.
    - label_b (string, default "Published"): background card label.
    - accent (green | blue | violet, default "blue"): focus highlight.

  Envelope (fixed IN/OUT, elastic HOLD only, never gsap.timeScale()):
    IN_BASE  = 1.32s  stage reveal, initial focus beat, then one 0.7s rack
    HOLD     = elastic card B remains sharp with a restrained depth drift
    OUT_BASE = 0.42s  completed focus state fades from the stage
    If D is shorter than IN_BASE plus OUT_BASE, both fixed phases compress
    proportionally and HOLD becomes zero. The rack still occurs exactly once.

  Mount contract: the runtime clones only this template. #root fills the host
  box, establishes the container query basis, has no data-width or data-height,
  and registers one paused timeline under the hardcoded focus-rack id.

          (function () {

                ? window.__hyperframes.getVariables()

            labelA.textContent = vars.label_a == null ? "Draft" : String(vars.label_a);

            var IN = IN_BASE * phaseScale;
            var OUT = OUT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var STAGE_IN = STAGE_IN_BASE * phaseScale;
            var RACK_AT = RACK_AT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var RACK_DURATION = RACK_DURATION_BASE * phaseScale;

                y: "-0.4cqh",

                rotation: 1.3,
```

# Focus Swap
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/components/focus-swap

Moves attention between two side-by-side cards as one recedes with scale, blur, and dimming while the other advances to full focus.

# Focus Swap

Moves attention between two side-by-side cards as one recedes with scale, blur, and dimming while the other advances to full focus.

**Focus Swap**

```html focus-swap.html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<!--
  focus-swap: HyperFrames video primitive (ui-props / holdable / demonstrate)

  Concept: attention moves between two side-by-side cards. The card losing
  focus recedes to 0.92 scale, softens, and dims while the other card advances
  to full scale, sharpness, and opacity. Both sides move together as one clean
  swap.

  Compiled-from evidence: launches-motion-vocabulary.md section 3.6 identifies
  blur-focus / defocus in 14 of 18 production launches and names focus-swap as
  a high-frequency missing primitive for blur + opacity + optional scale.

  Use when: directing the viewer from one product state, option, or result to
  another without moving either element out of its established layout.

  Variables:
    - focus ("a" | "b", default "b"): the card that ends focused.
    - blurPx (number, default 6): blur applied to the unfocused card.
    - dim (number from 0 to 1, default 0.5): unfocused card opacity.

  Envelope (holdable):
    IN = 0.90s at the standard duration, including a 0.20s readable lead.
    HOLD = elastic and deliberately still after focus lands.
    OUT = none; the host composition owns the cut or exit.
    For durations under 0.90s, the lead and swap compress to finish by D.

  Sync point: focus-landed at 0.90s into IN at the standard duration. It
  compresses with IN only when D is shorter than 0.90s and never enters HOLD.

  Sound: none. This continuous attention shift has no discrete impact cue.

  Mount contract: this is a template-wrapped sub-composition. The runtime
  clones only template contents. #root has no data-width or data-height and
  fills the host-owned box with position:absolute, inset:0, and
  container-type:size. The paused GSAP timeline is registered under the
  hardcoded composition id "focus-swap".
-->

  lang="en"
  data-composition-variables='[
    { "id": "focus", "type": "enum", "role": "motion", "label": "Final focus", "description": "Card that ends sharp, full-size, and fully opaque.", "default": "b", "options": [{ "value": "a", "label": "Card A" }, { "value": "b", "label": "Card B" }] },
    { "id": "blurPx", "type": "number", "role": "style", "label": "Unfocused blur", "description": "Blur applied to the card outside the viewer focus.", "default": 6, "min": 0, "max": 20, "step": 1, "unit": "px" },
    { "id": "dim", "type": "number", "role": "style", "label": "Unfocused opacity", "description": "Opacity of the card outside the viewer focus.", "default": 0.5, "min": 0, "max": 1, "step": 0.05 }
  ]'
>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <title>Focus Swap</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <template>
      <div id="root" data-composition-id="focus-swap" data-duration="1.5" data-fps="30">
        <style>
          *,
          *::before,
          *::after {
            box-sizing: border-box;
          }

          #root {
            position: absolute;
            inset: 0;
            container-type: size;
            isolation: isolate;
            overflow: hidden;
            background: var(--bg);
            color: var(--fg);

          .fs-clip {

        <div class="fs-clip clip" data-start="0" data-duration="1.5" data-track-index="0">
          <div class="fs-pair">
            <article class="fs-card" data-focus-card="a" aria-label="Card A, plan">
              <div class="fs-card-head">
                <span class="fs-card-letter">A</span>
                <span class="fs-status">Plan</span>
              </div>
              <div class="fs-copy">

                <div class="fs-meter-fill" style="--fs-meter-width: 58%"></div>
              </div>
            </article>

            <article class="fs-card" data-focus-card="b" aria-label="Card B, launch">
              <div class="fs-card-head">
                <span class="fs-card-letter">B</span>
                <span class="fs-status">Launch</span>
              </div>
              <div class="fs-copy">
                <h2 class="fs-title">Ship the result</h2>
                <p class="fs-detail">Move from approved work to live impact.</p>
              </div>
              <div class="fs-meter" aria-hidden="true">
                <div class="fs-meter-fill" style="--fs-meter-width: 86%"></div>
              </div>
            </article>
          </div>
        </div>

        <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
        <script>
          (function () {
            "use strict";

            var root = document.getElementById("root");
            var cardA = root.querySelector('[data-focus-card="a"]');
            var cardB = root.querySelector('[data-focus-card="b"]');
            var vars =
              window.__hyperframes && window.__hyperframes.getVariables
                ? window.__hyperframes.getVariables()
                : {};

            // INVARIANT: focus is the only owner of which card advances and
            // which recedes. Invalid input resolves to the declared default.
            var targetIsB = vars.focus !== "a";
            var initialFocused = targetIsB ? cardA : cardB;
            var targetFocused = targetIsB ? cardB : cardA;

            var rawBlur = Number(vars.blurPx);
            var blurPx = Number.isFinite(rawBlur) ? Math.max(0, Math.min(20, rawBlur)) : 6;
            var rawDim = Number(vars.dim);
            var dim = Number.isFinite(rawDim) ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1, rawDim)) : 0.5;
            var blurred = "blur(" + blurPx + "px)";
            var sharp = "blur(0px)";

            // RETIME RANGE: keep the standard 0.20s lead and 0.70s swap. Only
            // short host durations compress them so focus always lands by D.
            var duration = Math.max(0.001, parseFloat(root.dataset.duration || "1.5"));
            var SWAP_START = Math.min(0.2, duration * 0.2);
            var SWAP_DURATION = Math.min(0.7, Math.max(0.001, duration - SWAP_START));

            gsap.set(initialFocused, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, filter: sharp });
            gsap.set(targetFocused, { opacity: dim, scale: 0.92, filter: blurred });

            var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
            tl.to(
              initialFocused,
              {
                opacity: dim,
                scale: 0.92,
                filter: blurred,
                duration: SWAP_DURATION,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              SWAP_START,
            );
            tl.to(
              targetFocused,
              {
                opacity: 1,
                scale: 1,
                filter: sharp,
                duration: SWAP_DURATION,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              SWAP_START,
            );

            tl.seek(0);

            window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
            window.__timelines["focus-swap"] = tl;
          })();
        </script>
      </div>
    </template>
  </body>
</html>
```

Copy npx hyperframes add focus-swap to the clipboard

That writes one file: `compositions/components/focus-swap.html`.

## Paste it into your composition

Open `compositions/components/focus-swap.html` and copy what is inside into your own composition.

A component has no size or duration of its own. It takes both from the composition
you paste it into.

## Variables

Every one of these has a default, so the piece works untouched. Set the ones you
want to change on the element:

| Variable | Default | Accepts | What it does |
| - | - | - | - |
| `focus` | `b` | `a`, `b` | Card that ends sharp, full-size, and fully opaque. |
| `blurPx` | `6` | 0px to 20px, step 1px | Blur applied to the card outside the viewer focus. |
| `dim` | `0.5` | 0 to 1, step 0.05 | Opacity of the card outside the viewer focus. |

Set them with `data-variable-values` on the element that mounts it. These are the
defaults, so this behaves exactly like the preview above until you change one:

```html wrap theme={null}
<div
  data-composition-id="focus-swap"
  data-composition-src="compositions/components/focus-swap.html"
  data-variable-values='{"focus":"b","blurPx":6,"dim":0.5}'
></div>
```

Tagged `effect` `ui-props` `focus` `blur` `attention` `demonstrate`.

# Gesture Tap

A contact circle taps a mobile pill button, releases it into a new labeled accent state, and lifts away.

**Gesture Tap**

```html gesture-tap.html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<!--
  gesture-tap: HyperFrames video primitive (ui-props / interaction / demonstrate)

  Concept: a contact circle appears directly over a real pill button, presses
  it, releases it into a new state, then lifts away. One mechanic, one job:
  showing a decisive mobile tap response.

  Variables:
    - tap_label (string, default "Follow"): button label before release.
    - response_label (string, default "Following"): button label after release.
    - accent (enum, green | blue | violet, default green): response color.

  Envelope: fixed IN and OUT with elastic HOLD only.
    IN_BASE = 1.35s. The stage fades in, contact fades up at the target,
    presses, then releases. The label swap, accent response, and pulse share
    one release timestamp.
    HOLD = max(0, D - IN - OUT). Only this phase stretches for longer mounts.
    A barely visible card drift keeps the held state alive.
    OUT_BASE = 0.55s. The completed mobile state fades cleanly.
    If D is shorter than IN_BASE + OUT_BASE, IN and OUT compress together.

  Mount contract: the runtime clones only this template. #root fills the host
  box, establishes the container query basis, carries no data-width or
  data-height, and registers one paused timeline under the literal
  gesture-tap key.
-->
<html
  lang="en"
  data-composition-id="gesture-tap"
  data-composition-duration="3"
  data-composition-variables='[
    { "id": "tap_label", "type": "string", "role": "content", "label": "Tap label", "description": "Button label shown before the tap response.", "default": "Follow" },
    { "id": "response_label", "type": "string", "role": "content", "label": "Response label", "description": "Button label shown when the tap releases.", "default": "Following" },
    { "id": "accent", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Accent", "description": "Color used for the completed button state and response pulse.", "default": "green", "options": [{ "value": "green", "label": "Green" }, { "value": "blue", "label": "Blue" }, { "value": "violet", "label": "Violet" }] }
  ]'

          #root {

            opacity: 0;
            will-change: transform, opacity;

            position: relative;
            width: 46cqw;
            height: 78cqh;

            border-bottom: 0.12cqmin solid #e5e7eb;

            font-size: 2.1cqh;

            letter-spacing: 0.08em;
            text-transform: uppercase;
          }

          .gt-signal {

          }

          .gt-avatar {
            width: 12cqmin;
            aspect-ratio: 1;
            border-radius: 50%;
            background: linear-gradient(145deg, #e2e8f0, #cbd5e1);
            box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 0.8cqmin #ffffff;
          }

          .gt-name {
            max-width: 34cqw;
            overflow: hidden;

              inset 0 0 0 0.8cqmin rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12),
              0 1.2cqh 3cqh rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.28);
            opacity: 0;
            transform-origin: 50% 50%;
            will-change: transform, opacity;
          }
        </style>

        <div
          id="gesture-tap-clip"
          class="gt-clip clip"
          data-start="0"
          data-duration="3"
          data-track-index="0"
        >
          <div class="gt-stage">
            <article class="gt-phone" aria-label="Mobile profile card">
              <div class="gt-status">
                <span>Profile</span>
                <span class="gt-signal" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </div>
              <div class="gt-profile">
                <div class="gt-avatar" aria-hidden="true"></div>
                <div class="gt-name">Maya Chen</div>
                <div class="gt-detail">Product designer sharing practical interaction notes.</div>
              </div>

                <button class="gt-button" type="button" aria-pressed="false" tabindex="-1">
                  <span class="gt-button-label"></span>
                </button>
                <div class="gt-contact" aria-hidden="true"></div>
              </div>
            </article>
          </div>
        </div>

        <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
        <script>
          (function () {
            "use strict";

            var root = document.getElementById("root");
            var stage = root.querySelector(".gt-stage");
            var card = root.querySelector(".gt-phone");
            var button = root.querySelector(".gt-button");
            var label = root.querySelector(".gt-button-label");
            var contact = root.querySelector(".gt-contact");
            var pulse = root.querySelector(".gt-response-pulse");
            var vars =
              window.__hyperframes && window.__hyperframes.getVariables
                ? window.__hyperframes.getVariables()
                : {};

            var tapLabel = vars.tap_label == null ? "Follow" : String(vars.tap_label);
            var responseLabel =
              vars.response_label == null ? "Following" : String(vars.response_label);
            var accentName =
              vars.accent === "blue" || vars.accent === "violet" ? vars.accent : "green";
            var accentColors = {
              green: "var(--brand, #34d399)",
              blue: "var(--accent, #60a5fa)",
              violet: "var(--accent-2, #a78bfa)",
            };
            var accentColor = accentColors[accentName];

            label.textContent = tapLabel;
            button.setAttribute("aria-label", tapLabel);
            root.style.setProperty("--gt-accent", accentColor);
            // GSAP interpolates colors numerically, so tween values need the
            // substituted color rather than the var() form.
            accentColor = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue("--gt-accent").trim();

            var IN_BASE = 1.35;
            var OUT_BASE = 0.55;
            var STAGE_IN_BASE = 0.24;
            var CONTACT_AT_BASE = 0.28;
            var CONTACT_IN_BASE = 0.18;
            var PRESS_AT_BASE = 0.54;
            var PRESS_DURATION_BASE = 0.18;
            var RELEASE_AT_BASE = 0.72;
            var RELEASE_DURATION_BASE = 0.28;
            var CONTACT_OUT_BASE = 0.34;
            var PULSE_DURATION_BASE = 0.56;

            var parsedDuration = Number.parseFloat(root.dataset.duration);
            var duration =
              Number.isFinite(parsedDuration) && parsedDuration > 0 ? parsedDuration : 3;
            var fixedBase = IN_BASE + OUT_BASE;
            var phaseScale = duration < fixedBase ? duration / fixedBase : 1;
            var IN = IN_BASE * phaseScale;
            var OUT = OUT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var HOLD = Math.max(0, duration - IN - OUT);
            var HOLD_START = IN;
            var OUT_START = IN + HOLD;
            var STAGE_IN = STAGE_IN_BASE * phaseScale;
            var CONTACT_AT = CONTACT_AT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var CONTACT_IN = CONTACT_IN_BASE * phaseScale;
            var PRESS_AT = PRESS_AT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var PRESS_DURATION = PRESS_DURATION_BASE * phaseScale;
            var RELEASE_AT = RELEASE_AT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var RELEASE_DURATION = RELEASE_DURATION_BASE * phaseScale;
            var CONTACT_OUT = CONTACT_OUT_BASE * phaseScale;
            var PULSE_DURATION = PULSE_DURATION_BASE * phaseScale;

            var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

            tl.to(stage, { opacity: 1, duration: STAGE_IN, ease: "power2.out" }, 0);

            // IN: the contact appears at the target. No x or y tween precedes the press.
            tl.fromTo(
              contact,
              { opacity: 0, scale: 0.82 },
              { opacity: 0.68, scale: 1, duration: CONTACT_IN, ease: "power2.out" },
              CONTACT_AT,
            );
            tl.to(
              button,
              {
                scale: 0.93,
                backgroundColor: "#26324a",
                duration: PRESS_DURATION,
                ease: "power4.in",
              },
              PRESS_AT,
            );
            tl.to(contact, { scale: 0.78, duration: PRESS_DURATION, ease: "power4.in" }, PRESS_AT);

            // Release owns the response. Label, state, accent fill, and pulse
            // all begin at RELEASE_AT so the UI answers on the release frame.
            tl.set(label, { innerText: responseLabel }, RELEASE_AT);
            tl.set(
              button,
              { attr: { "aria-label": responseLabel, "aria-pressed": "true" } },
              RELEASE_AT,
            );
            tl.to(
              button,
              {
                scale: 1,
                backgroundColor: accentColor,
                borderColor: accentColor,
                color: "#071015",
                duration: RELEASE_DURATION,
                ease: "back.out(1.7)",
              },
              RELEASE_AT,
            );
            tl.set(pulse, { opacity: 0.58, scale: 0.76 }, RELEASE_AT);
            tl.to(
              pulse,
              { opacity: 0, scale: 1.14, duration: PULSE_DURATION, ease: "power2.out" },
              RELEASE_AT,
            );
            tl.to(
              contact,
              {
                opacity: 0,
                scale: 1.04,
                y: "-5cqh",
                duration: CONTACT_OUT,
                ease: "power2.in",
              },
              RELEASE_AT,
            );

            // HOLD: only this phase stretches. One slow yoyo returns the card
            // to its resting position exactly when OUT starts.
            if (HOLD > 0) {
              tl.to(
                card,
                {
                  y: "-0.6cqh",
                  duration: HOLD / 2,
                  ease: "sine.inOut",
                  yoyo: true,
                  repeat: 1,
                },
                HOLD_START,
              );
            }

            // OUT: the completed state remains intact while the stage exits.
            tl.to(stage, { opacity: 0, y: "-1.4cqh", duration: OUT, ease: "power2.in" }, OUT_START);

            tl.seek(0);
            window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
            window.__timelines["gesture-tap"] = tl;
          })();
        </script>
      </div>
    </template>
  </body>
</html>
```

# Gloss Sweep
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/components/gloss-sweep

A card lands with a restrained slam, catches one diagonal specular gloss, and holds perfectly still.

# Gloss Sweep

A card lands with a restrained slam, catches one diagonal specular gloss, and holds perfectly still.

**Gloss Sweep**

```html gloss-sweep.html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<!--
  gloss-sweep: HyperFrames video primitive (celebrations / payoff)

  Concept: a compact card lands with a restrained slam, receives one
  diagonal specular sweep, then holds perfectly still. The gloss is the
  whole celebration. There is no pulse, confetti, drift, or exit.

  Variables:
    - text (string, default "Pro"): the card label.
    - accent (green | blue | violet, default green): the card color.
    - sweep_angle (number, default 25): gloss angle in degrees.

  Envelope (fixed IN, elastic HOLD, no OUT):
    IN_BASE  = 1.35s, small landing followed by one gloss sweep
    HOLD     = elastic = max(0, D - IN_BASE), completely still
    OUT_BASE = 0s, the card remains in its confident resting state
    If D is shorter than IN_BASE, the landing and sweep compress together.

  Mount contract: the runtime clones only this template. #root fills the
  host box, establishes the container query basis, has no data-width or

          (function () {
            "use strict";

            var root = document.getElementById("root");

              window.__hyperframes && window.__hyperframes.getVariables
                ? window.__hyperframes.getVariables()
                : {};

            var accents = {
              green: {
                surface: "#123b2c",
                surfaceBright: "#1a513c",

            var palette = accents[accent];

            var angleValue = Number(vars.sweep_angle);
            var sweepAngle = Number.isFinite(angleValue)
              ? Math.max(-60, Math.min(60, angleValue))
              : 25;

            label.textContent = text;
            card.style.setProperty("--gs-surface", palette.surface);
            card.style.setProperty("--gs-surface-bright", palette.surfaceBright);
            card.style.setProperty("--gs-edge", palette.edge);
            card.style.setProperty("--gs-label", palette.label);
            gloss.style.setProperty("--gs-angle", sweepAngle + "deg");

            var IN_BASE = 1.35;
            var LAND_BASE = 0.5;
            var SWEEP_AT_BASE = 0.65;
            var SWEEP_BASE = 0.7;
            var duration = Math.max(0.001, parseFloat(root.dataset.duration || "2.5"));
            var scale = duration < IN_BASE ? duration / IN_BASE : 1;
            var LAND = LAND_BASE * scale;
            var SWEEP_AT = SWEEP_AT_BASE * scale;
            var SWEEP = SWEEP_BASE * scale;

            var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

            tl.fromTo(
              card,
              { y: "-5cqh", scale: 1.06 },
              { y: "0cqh", scale: 1, duration: LAND, ease: "expo.out" },
              0,
            );
            tl.set(gloss, { opacity: 1, "--gs-sweep": -30 }, SWEEP_AT);
            tl.to(gloss, { "--gs-sweep": 130, duration: SWEEP, ease: "power2.out" }, SWEEP_AT);
            tl.set(gloss, { opacity: 0 }, SWEEP_AT + SWEEP);
            tl.seek(0);

            window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
            window.__timelines["gloss-sweep"] = tl;
          })();
        </script>
      </div>
    </template>
  </body>
```

Copy npx hyperframes add gloss-sweep to the clipboard

That writes one file: `compositions/components/gloss-sweep.html`.

## Paste it into your composition

Open `compositions/components/gloss-sweep.html` and copy what is inside into your own composition.

A component has no size or duration of its own. It takes both from the composition
you paste it into.

## Variables

Every one of these has a default, so the piece works untouched. Set the ones you
want to change on the element:

| Variable | Default | Accepts | What it does |
| - | - | - | - |
| `text` | `Pro` | string | Text displayed on the card. |
| `accent` | `green` | `green`, `blue`, `violet` | Color treatment for the card. |
| `sweep_angle` | `25` | -60deg to 60deg, step 1deg | Angle of the specular gloss in degrees. |

Set them with `data-variable-values` on the element that mounts it. These are the
defaults, so this behaves exactly like the preview above until you change one:

```html wrap theme={null}
<div
  data-composition-id="gloss-sweep"
  data-composition-src="compositions/components/gloss-sweep.html"
  data-variable-values='{"text":"Pro","accent":"green","sweep_angle":25}'
></div>
```

Tagged `motion-primitive` `celebration` `gloss` `card` `badge` `payoff`.

# Grade Split Reveal

# Grade Split Reveal

The same picture twice, one flat and one finished, with a hard edge sweeping between them. It stops in the middle long enough to compare, then commits and the graded look takes the frame. Both looks are real HyperFrames color grading run through the WebGL shader, so the preview and the render match.

**Grade Split Reveal**

```html grade-split-reveal.html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<!--
  grade-split-reveal: the grade arrives as a moving edge.

  Two copies of the same plate sit exactly on top of each other. The lower copy carries a
  flat, milky look, the way ungraded footage comes off a camera. The upper copy carries the
  finished warm cinematic look. A hard edge sweeps across the upper copy, so the graded
  version eats the flat one from left to right and you read both halves of the same picture
  at the same time. It pauses in the middle long enough for the eye to compare, then commits
  and takes the whole frame.

  Both looks are real HyperFrames color grading, not a CSS filter. The runtime hands each
  image to a WebGL shader and swaps in a graded canvas, and the render pipeline redraws the
  same shader, so what you preview is what encodes. Color grading is media only: it applies
  to <video> and <img>, never to text, SVG or ordinary DOM.

  The plate here is a procedural SVG scene built in this file, so the primitive is
  deterministic and ships nothing licensed. Replace PLATE_SRC with your own photo or a video
  poster and the whole move still works. Swap AFTER_GRADE for any preset id or hand written
  adjust block.

  The edge itself is never animated with clip-path. The upper copy lives in a wrapper with
  overflow hidden and the wrapper's width is what moves, so the sweep is one plain numeric
  tween that seeks perfectly and never re-parses a string.

  Every ease is a cubic bezier written out by hand and solved in this file. No preset is used
  anywhere.

  Variables. Each one is read once at mount, falls back to its declared default on anything
  missing or unrecognised, and changes what lands on screen. Timing is untouched: same six
  seconds, same 30fps, same beats.

    - look (warm-cinematic | cool-teal | bleach-bypass, default warm-cinematic): the grade the
      upper copy carries, and the label printed over it. All three are real grading blocks
      handed to the shader, not CSS filters.
    - split (25 to 85, default 62, percent of the plate width): where the edge stops to hold
      the comparison before it commits and takes the rest.
    - edge (hairline | bold | hidden, default hairline): the divider line riding the wipe.
      hidden removes it, so the grade arrives with no visible seam.
    - labels (on | off, default on): the two captions naming each half of the plate.

  Mount contract: everything lives inside <template>, styles and scripts included, and the
  scripts sit INSIDE the composition root. A host clones template content into its own mount
  and only runs scripts found inside the root; markup left outside is copied without its
  behaviour, which renders a black card with no timeline at all.
-->
<html
  lang="en"
  data-composition-variables='[
    { "id": "look", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Look", "description": "Grade carried by the upper copy, and the label printed over it.     { "id": "split", "type": "number", "role": "motion", "label": "Split point", "description": "How far across the plate the edge stops to hold the comparison, before it commits and takes the rest.", "default": 62, "min": 25, "max": 85, "step": 1, "unit": "%" },
    { "id": "edge", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Edge", "description": "The divider line riding the wipe. Hidden drops it entirely so the grade arrives with no seam.", "default": "hairline", "options": [{ "value": "hairline", "label": "Hairline" }, { "value": "bold", "label": "Bold" }, { "value": "hidden", "label": "Hidden" }] },
    { "id": "labels", "type": "enum", "role": "style", "label": "Labels", "description": "Show or hide the two captions naming each half of the plate.", "default": "on", "options": [{ "value": "on", "label": "Show" }, { "value": "off", "label": "Hide" }] }
  ]'
>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <title>Grade Split Reveal</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <template>
      <div
        id="root"
        class="clip gs-root"
        data-composition-id="grade-split-reveal"
        data-duration="6"
        data-fps="30"
      >
        <style>
          [data-composition-id="grade-split-reveal"] {
            --ink: #f6f4ef;
            --rule: rgba(246, 244, 239, 0.55);
            position: absolute;
            inset: 0;
            overflow: hidden;
            background: transparent;
            pointer-events: none;
          }

            position: absolute;
            overflow: hidden;
            border-radius: 10px;

            left: 0;

            height: 100%;
            overflow: hidden;

          .gs-layer img {
            display: block;
            object-fit: cover;
          }

            position: absolute;
            top: 0;
            left: 0;
            width: 2px;
            height: 100%;
            background: var(--ink);
            box-shadow: 0 0 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7);
          }
          .gs-tag {
            position: absolute;
            font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
            font-weight: 700;
            text-transform: uppercase;
            letter-spacing: 0.16em;
            color: var(--ink);
            opacity: 0;
            white-space: nowrap;
            text-shadow: 0 2px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85);

        </style>

        <div id="gs-plate">
          <div class="gs-layer" id="gs-before"><img id="gs-img-before" alt="" /></div>
          <div class="gs-layer" id="gs-after"><img id="gs-img-after" alt="" /></div>
          <div id="gs-edge"></div>
          <div class="gs-tag" id="gs-tag-before">Ungraded</div>
          <div class="gs-tag" id="gs-tag-after">Warm Cinematic</div>
        </div>

        <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
        <script>
          (function () {
            gsap.defaults({ immediateRender: false });

            /* Cubic bezier solved by hand. Newton first, bisection when the slope dies. */
            function bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) {
              function curve(t, a1, a2) {
                var A = 1 - 3 * a2 + 3 * a1;
                var B = 3 * a2 - 6 * a1;
                var C = 3 * a1;
                return ((A * t + B) * t + C) * t;
              }
              function slope(t, a1, a2) {
                var A = 1 - 3 * a2 + 3 * a1;
                var B = 3 * a2 - 6 * a1;
                var C = 3 * a1;
                return (3 * A * t + 2 * B) * t + C;
              }
              return function (p) {
                if (p <= 0) return 0;
                if (p >= 1) return 1;
                var t = p;
                for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
                  var d = slope(t, x1, x2);
                  if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-6) break;
                  var e = curve(t, x1, x2) - p;
                  if (Math.abs(e) < 1e-7) return curve(t, y1, y2);
                  t -= e / d;
                }
                var lo = 0;
                var hi = 1;
                t = p;
                for (var j = 0; j < 24; j++) {
                  var x = curve(t, x1, x2);
                  if (Math.abs(x - p) < 1e-7) break;
                  if (x > p) hi = t;
                  else lo = t;
                  t = (lo + hi) / 2;
                }
                return curve(t, y1, y2);
              };
            }

            /* Plate settles, never bounces. */
            var EASE_PLATE = bezier(0.16, 0.84, 0.24, 1);
            /* The sweep loiters, then finishes fast, the way a hand drags a compare slider. */
            var EASE_WIPE = bezier(0.62, 0, 0.14, 1);
            /* The commit is decisive from the first frame. */
            var EASE_COMMIT = bezier(0.4, 0, 0.05, 1);
            var EASE_TAG = bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.3, 1);
            var EASE_FADE = bezier(0.4, 0, 0.7, 1);

            var DUR = 6;

            /* ---- the plate. Swap PLATE_SRC for your own photo or video poster. ---- */
            var SCENE =
              /* width and height are not decoration. An SVG served to an <img> with only a
                 viewBox has no intrinsic size, and a texture upload from it comes back
                 empty, so the shader grades a blank plate. */
              '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1600" height="900" viewBox="0 0 1600 900">' +
              "<defs>" +
              '<linearGradient id="sky" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">' +
              '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#1b2340"/><stop offset="0.42" stop-color="#5b4a63"/>' +
              '<stop offset="0.68" stop-color="#c8794a"/><stop offset="0.78" stop-color="#f0a75c"/>' +
              '<stop offset="1" stop-color="#f7c988"/></linearGradient>' +
              '<linearGradient id="sea" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">' +
              '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#c98a55"/><stop offset="0.3" stop-color="#6a5560"/>' +
              '<stop offset="1" stop-color="#1a1d30"/></linearGradient>' +
              '<radialGradient id="glow" cx="0.62" cy="0.74" r="0.42">' +
              '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#ffdfa8" stop-opacity="0.9"/>' +
              '<stop offset="1" stop-color="#ffdfa8" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient>' +
              "</defs>" +
              '<rect width="1600" height="900" fill="url(#sky)"/>' +
              '<rect width="1600" height="900" fill="url(#glow)"/>' +
              '<circle cx="992" cy="660" r="58" fill="#fff0cd"/>' +
              '<path d="M0 640 L250 578 L430 618 L640 552 L820 606 L1010 566 L1240 620 L1430 578 L1600 616 L1600 700 L0 700 Z" fill="#3a2f45"/>' +
              '<path d="M0 668 L210 634 L400 664 L610 622 L840 662 L1080 630 L1330 668 L1600 638 L1600 700 L0 700 Z" fill="#2a2337"/>' +
              '<rect y="700" width="1600" height="200" fill="url(#sea)"/>' +
              '<rect x="962" y="700" width="60" height="200" fill="#ffdfa8" opacity="0.42"/>' +
              '<rect x="978" y="700" width="28" height="200" fill="#fff3d4" opacity="0.5"/>' +
              '<g fill="#f4e3c2" opacity="0.34">' +
              '<rect x="120" y="742" width="1360" height="3"/><rect x="240" y="786" width="1120" height="3"/>' +
              '<rect x="60" y="828" width="1480" height="4"/><rect x="300" y="868" width="1000" height="4"/></g>' +
              '<g fill="#e8d3b4" opacity="0.5">' +
              '<rect x="180" y="330" width="420" height="7" rx="3"/><rect x="300" y="372" width="260" height="6" rx="3"/>' +

              '<path d="M0 760 L118 700 L268 760 L268 900 L0 900 Z" fill="#12121e"/>' +
              '<path d="M1600 742 L1462 700 L1318 742 L1318 900 L1600 900 Z" fill="#0f0f1a"/>' +
              "</svg>";

              preset: "neutral",

            }

            var LOOKS = {
              "warm-cinematic": { label: "Warm Cinematic", grade: AFTER_GRADE },
              "cool-teal": {
                label: "Cool Teal",
                grade: {
                  preset: "deep-contrast",
                  intensity: 1,

              },
            };
            var LOOK = LOOKS[pick(LOOKS, vars.look, "warm-cinematic")];

            var EDGE_WIDTHS = { hairline: "2px", bold: "6px", hidden: "0px" };
            var EDGE = pick(EDGE_WIDTHS, vars.edge, "hairline");

            /* A number arrives as a number from --variables, but a hand written override can
               still be a string or nonsense. parseFloat plus a range test covers both. */
            var SPLIT = parseFloat(vars.split);
            if (!isFinite(SPLIT) || SPLIT < 25 || SPLIT > 85) SPLIT = 62;

            var LABELS_ON = vars.labels !== "off";

            var root = document.getElementById("gs-plate").parentElement;
            var FRAME_W = root.clientWidth || 1920;
            var FRAME_H = root.clientHeight || 1080;

            /* The plate keeps the frame's own shape, inset by a constant margin, so one file
               reads correctly in landscape, portrait and square. */
            var INSET = Math.min(FRAME_W, FRAME_H) * 0.085;
            var PW = Math.round(FRAME_W - INSET * 2);
            var PH = Math.round(FRAME_H - INSET * 2);

            var plate = document.getElementById("gs-plate");
            plate.style.left = INSET + "px";
            plate.style.top = INSET + "px";
            plate.style.width = PW + "px";
            plate.style.height = PH + "px";

            var before = document.getElementById("gs-before");
            var after = document.getElementById("gs-after");
            var edge = document.getElementById("gs-edge");
            var tagBefore = document.getElementById("gs-tag-before");
            var tagAfter = document.getElementById("gs-tag-after");

            /* Both images are laid out at the full plate width. Only the wrapper narrows, so
               the shader canvas the runtime drops in keeps its measured box and the edge is a
               clean crop rather than a squeeze. */
            [
              [document.getElementById("gs-img-before"), BEFORE_GRADE],
              [document.getElementById("gs-img-after"), LOOK.grade],
            ].forEach(function (pair) {
              pair[0].style.width = PW + "px";
              pair[0].style.height = PH + "px";
              pair[0].setAttribute("data-color-grading", JSON.stringify(pair[1]));
              pair[0].src = PLATE_SRC;
            });
            before.style.width = PW + "px";

            var TAG = Math.max(11, Math.round(Math.min(FRAME_W, FRAME_H) * 0.019));
            var PAD = Math.round(INSET * 0.62);
            [tagBefore, tagAfter].forEach(function (t) {
              t.style.fontSize = TAG + "px";
              t.style.bottom = PAD + "px";
            });
            /* The graded copy grows from the left, so its label sits on the left. Putting
               these the other way round labels each half with the look it is not. */
            tagAfter.style.left = PAD + "px";
            tagBefore.style.right = PAD + "px";
            tagBefore.style.textAlign = "right";

            tagAfter.textContent = LOOK.label;
            edge.style.width = EDGE_WIDTHS[EDGE];
            /* The edge also casts a shadow, so zero width alone would leave a smudge. */
            if (EDGE === "hidden") edge.style.display = "none";
            if (!LABELS_ON) {
              tagBefore.style.display = "none";
              tagAfter.style.display = "none";
            }

            /* Rest state lives outside the timeline so frame zero is already correct. */
            /* The plate is lit at frame zero and arrives on scale alone. Fading it up from
               nothing would leave the first frames of the clip literally blank, which reads
               as a broken card in any grid of thumbnails. */
            gsap.set(plate, { transformOrigin: "50% 50%", scale: 1.05, opacity: 1 });
            gsap.set(after, { width: 0 });
            gsap.set(edge, { x: 0, opacity: 0 });
            gsap.set([tagBefore, tagAfter], { opacity: 0, y: 10 });

            var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

            /* The plate arrives. */
            tl.fromTo(plate, { scale: 1.05 }, { scale: 1, duration: 0.62, ease: EASE_PLATE }, 0);
            tl.fromTo(
              tagBefore,
              { opacity: 0, y: 10 },
              { opacity: 0.82, y: 0, duration: 0.34, ease: EASE_TAG },
              0.36,
            );

            /* The grade sweeps in and stops short, so both halves are readable together. */
            var HOLD = Math.round(PW * (SPLIT / 100));
            tl.fromTo(after, { width: 0 }, { width: HOLD, duration: 1.6, ease: EASE_WIPE }, 0.7);
            tl.fromTo(edge, { x: 0 }, { x: HOLD, duration: 1.6, ease: EASE_WIPE }, 0.7);
            tl.fromTo(edge, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.2, ease: EASE_FADE }, 0.7);
            tl.fromTo(
              tagAfter,
              { opacity: 0, y: 10 },
              { opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.34, ease: EASE_TAG },
              1.16,
            );

            /* Then it commits and takes the whole plate. */
            tl.fromTo(after, { width: HOLD }, { width: PW, duration: 1.2, ease: EASE_COMMIT }, 3.1);
            tl.fromTo(edge, { x: HOLD }, { x: PW, duration: 1.2, ease: EASE_COMMIT }, 3.1);
            tl.fromTo(
              tagBefore,
              { opacity: 0.82 },
              { opacity: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: EASE_FADE },
              3.1,
            );
            tl.fromTo(edge, { opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.3, ease: EASE_FADE }, 4.05);
            /* A small push in lands the finished look instead of just stopping on it. */
            tl.fromTo(plate, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.03, duration: 1.5, ease: EASE_COMMIT }, 3.1);

            tl.set({}, {}, DUR);
            tl.seek(0);

            window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
            window.__timelines["grade-split-reveal"] = tl;
          })();
        </script>
      </div>
    </template>
  </body>
</html>
```

## Variables

Every one of these has a default, so the piece works untouched. Set the ones you
want to change on the element:

| Variable | Default | Accepts | What it does |
| - | - | - | - |
| `look` | `warm-cinematic` | `warm-cinematic`, `cool-teal`, `bleach-bypass` | Grade carried by the upper copy, and the label printed over it. All three are real grading blocks handed to the shader, not CSS filters. |
| `split` | `62` | 25% to 85%, step 1% | How far across the plate the edge stops to hold the comparison, before it commits and takes the rest. |
| `edge` | `hairline` | `hairline`, `bold`, `hidden` | The divider line riding the wipe. Hidden drops it entirely so the grade arrives with no seam. |
| `labels` | `on` | `on`, `off` | Show or hide the two captions naming each half of the plate. |

Set them with `data-variable-values` on the element that mounts it. These are the
defaults, so this behaves exactly like the preview above until you change one:

```html wrap theme={null}
<div
  data-composition-id="grade-split-reveal"
  data-composition-src="compositions/components/grade-split-reveal.html"
  data-variable-values='{"look":"warm-cinematic","split":62,"edge":"hairline","labels":"on"}'
></div>
```
