| `highpass` | `frequency` 20–20000 Hz (300, log) **AUTO** · `q` 0.1–20 (0.707, log) **AUTO** · `poles` `1`\|`2` (2) |
| `lowpass` | `frequency` 100–20000 Hz (8000, log) **AUTO** · `q` 0.1–20 (0.707, log) **AUTO** · `poles` `1`\|`2` (2) |
| `peaking` | `frequency` 20–20000 Hz (1000, log) **AUTO** · `gain` −40–40 dB (0) **AUTO** · `q` 0.1–20 (1, log) **AUTO** |
| `lowshelf` | `frequency` 20–2000 Hz (200, log) **AUTO** · `gain` −40–40 dB (0) **AUTO** |
| `highshelf` | `frequency` 500–20000 Hz (4000, log) **AUTO** · `gain` −40–40 dB (0) **AUTO** |

`q` is bandwidth — higher is narrower. `poles` is the slope: `2` is the usual
biquad (12 dB/oct), `1` is gentler (6 dB/oct). Shelving filters have no `q`; the
Web Audio spec leaves it unused for them.

### Dynamics — how level behaves over time

| Effect | Parameters |
| - | - |
| `gain` | `gain` −60–12 dB (0) **AUTO** |
| `compressor` | `threshold` −60–0 dB (−24) · `ratio` 1–20 (4) · `attack` 0.01–2000 ms (20, log) · `release` 0.01–9000 ms (250, log) · `knee` 1–8 (2.83) · `makeup` 0–36 dB (0) · `mix` 0–1 (1) |
| `limiter` | `limit` −24–0 dB (−1) · `attack` 0.1–80 ms (5) · `release` 1–8000 ms (50, log) · `level_out` −24–24 dB (0) |
| `truepeak` | `ceiling` −24–0 dBTP (−1) · `lookahead` 0.5–10 ms (3) · `release` 10–2000 ms (80, log) |
| `gate` | `threshold` −80–0 dB (−35) · `range` −80–0 dB (−24) · `ratio` 1–20 (10) · `attack` 0.01–9000 ms (1, log) · `release` 0.01–9000 ms (100, log) · `knee` 1–8 (2.83) |

Cuts on `gain` reach −60 dB, boosts stop at +12: it is a level stage for making
room, and a chain that could add 40 dB would clip long before that was useful.
`knee` of 1 is a hard corner. `mix` below 1 blends the dry signal back in
(parallel compression). `range` is how far down the gate pulls when closed.

`limiter` is an envelope follower: it reacts to the level of the signal, has no
lookahead, and can let a sample peak or an inter-sample peak through. `truepeak`
is the one to use for a delivery ceiling. It estimates the true peak on a 4x
oversampled signal, reads `lookahead` ms ahead so the gain is already down when
the peak arrives, and holds that estimate at `ceiling`. Channels share one
gain. It delays its output by `lookahead` plus about 0.3 ms (3.3 to 10.3 ms across
the range): the offline render trims that delay, live preview plays it, so the
sound is that much behind the picture. A seek clears the limiter's delay line and
held gain on a group or master bus. Changing `lookahead` rebuilds the node.

The ceiling is held against that 4x estimate, not against the waveform itself. A
4x interpolator cannot see the peaks of content close to Nyquist, so the true peak
can end above `ceiling`. Measured against an ideal 16x interpolation, tones, pink
noise and a dense mix ended at most 0.6 dB over. Full-band white noise driven 8 dB
or more into the limiter ended 1.2 to 1.7 dB over (median 1.4 dB, 28 runs of 10
to 30 s). A meter that also reads at 4x, such as ffmpeg's `ebur128=peak=true`,
reports that same noise about 0.1 dB over, so it will not show the miss. Under a
hard delivery limit set `ceiling` at least 2 dB below it: −3 dBTP for a −1 dBTP
limit.

### Nonlinear — changes the waveform's shape

| Effect | Parameters |
| - | - |
| `saturate` | `type` `tanh`\|`atan`\|`cubic`\|`exp`\|`alg`\|`quintic`\|`sin`\|`erf`\|`hard` (tanh) · `threshold` −40–0 dB (−6) · `output` −24–24 dB (0) **AUTO** · `oversample` 1–8× (4) |
| `bitcrush` | `bits` 1–32 (8) · `samples` 1–250× (1) · `mix` 0–1 (1) |

`tanh` is the gentlest curve, `hard` is outright clipping. Higher `oversample`
costs more CPU and keeps aliasing down. `samples` repeats each sample N times — a
crude downsample, which is where the lo-fi character comes from.

### Time — where a track sits, and how it moves

| Effect | Parameters |
| - | - |
| `delay` | `time` 1–5000 ms (250, log) **AUTO** · `feedback` 0.01–0.95 (0.35) **AUTO** · `mix` 0–1 (0.4) **AUTO** |
| `reverb` | `size` 0.05–1 (0.7) · `damping` 0–1 (0.5) · `wet` 0–1 (0.35) **AUTO** · `dry` 0–1 (0.7) **AUTO** |
| `chorus` | `delay` 1–100 ms (7) **AUTO** · `depth` 0–10 ms (2) **AUTO** · `speed` 0.01–10 Hz (1) **AUTO** · `mix` 0–1 (0.5) **AUTO** |
| `phaser` | `in_gain` 0–1 (0.4) **AUTO** · `out_gain` 0–2 (0.74) **AUTO** · `delay` 0.1–5 ms (3) · `decay` 0–0.99 (0.4) · `speed` 0.1–2 Hz (0.5) **AUTO** · `type` `0`\|`1` (0) |
| `pitchshift` | `semitones` −12–12 st (0, whole steps) · `mix` 0–1 (1) |

`pitchshift` moves pitch without changing playback speed, which is what
separates it from a playback-rate change. Neither of its parameters can be
automated — it is a worklet.

Reverb convolves a *generated* impulse and both preview and render generate the
same one, so a room is reproducible without shipping an impulse file. Higher
`damping` rolls the top off the tail faster. `feedback` is bounded below 1
because at 1 it never decays.

## Why some parameters cannot be automated

Automation is handed to the audio thread once, as native `AudioParam` ramps and
curves — that is what keeps it sample-accurate and identical between preview and
render. A parameter can therefore only be automated if an `AudioParam` backs it.
Three kinds do not:

| Kind | Effects | Consequence |
| - | - | - |
| Worklet processor options | `compressor`, `limiter`, `truepeak`, `gate`, `bitcrush`, `pitchshift` | **No parameter is automatable at all** |
| A WaveShaper curve | `saturate`'s `type`, `threshold`, `oversample` | Only its `output` stage is a real param |
| A convolution impulse | `reverb`'s `size`, `damping` | `wet` / `dry` are gain stages and automate fine |

**A lane on a non-automatable parameter is silently inert.** To make one of those
behave differently over time, automate a `gain` stage around it instead: a lane
on a `gain` before a compressor changes how hard the compressor is driven, which
is most of what automating its threshold would have done.

## Presets, jobs, and one-knob profiles

Every one of these is a shortcut to a chain you could have built by hand. Open
any of them and you find ordinary effects with their parameters showing.

### Presets

Twenty-two, in four families. Applying one **appends**; re-applying one already
present replaces its own nodes in place, because position is signal order.

| Family | Ids |
| - | - |
| Voice | `voice-clean`, `voice-broadcast`, `voice-warm` |
| Repair | `rumble-cut`, `room-gate`, `boom-tame`, `harsh-tame` |
| Character | `telephone`, `radio-am`, `megaphone`, `lofi-tape`, `pa-system`, `intercom`, `doofus-worble`, `chipmunk`, `giant`, `monster` |
| Space | `room-tight`, `room-natural`, `hall`, `slap-echo`, `dub-throw` |

`chipmunk`, `giant`, and `monster` are built on `pitchshift`, so they change the
speaker rather than the channel.

`voice-clean` is Remove Rumble → Reduce Mud → Even Out Loudness → Add Clarity →
Peak Ceiling. `voice-broadcast` is denser and more forward; `voice-warm` adds
body rather than cutting it.

A preset's nodes are wrapped in a wet/dry blend, so `presetAmount` (0–1) fades
the whole thing, and `fx.preset.<id>` is an automation target that ramps it over
time. That is the only way to automate a preset as a unit — its nodes share no
common parameter.

### Jobs

Five named `peaking` filters with the frequency already chosen. Picking the job
is picking the range, which is what makes a single "how much" knob honest.

| Job | Symptom | Sets |
| - | - | - |
| Tame Boominess | Too much chest — it booms | 200 Hz, −4 dB, Q 1.4 |
| Reduce Mud | Muffled, like it is behind cardboard | 250 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1.2 |
| Reduce Boxiness | Sounds like a small room, or a box | 400 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1.4 |
| Add Clarity | Words are hard to make out | 3 kHz, +2.5 dB, Q 1 |
| Soften Harshness | Harsh and tiring to listen to | 3.2 kHz, −3 dB, Q 1.6 |

Writing one by hand, carry the name in `label` — the parameters alone are not
the job.

**Every job also ships inside a preset at identical settings**, which is where
the five came from. So check what a preset already contains before adding a job
on top: `voice-clean` plus a Reduce Mud job is −6 dB at 250 Hz where −3 was
meant.

### One-knob profiles

Five effects have no single parameter that can honestly be their face — a
compressor's threshold means nothing without its ratio. They get a derived
control instead, 0–1, setting several parameters together.

| Effect | Knob | 0 → 1 | Sets |
| - | - | - | - |
| `compressor` | Evenness | Barely touched → very even, quite squashed | threshold, ratio, attack, release, makeup |
| `gate` | Tightness | Only true silence → cuts quiet words too | threshold, range, release |
| `saturate` | Warmth | Just a sheen → openly distorted | threshold, output |
| `reverb` | Space | A small tight room → a big open hall | size, wet, dry |
| `bitcrush` | Crush | Slightly gritty → destroyed | bits, samples, mix |

Evenness, Warmth, and Space are **level-matched**: the make-up gain, output trim,
and dry leg move with the drive, so turning the knob up does not also turn the
track up. Tightness and Crush are not, because neither has a trim to move.

The chain stores the mechanism values, not the knob position — the knob is read
back by inverting the curve, so hand-editing a parameter under a profile is
allowed and simply moves the knob.

## Voiceover carve

A carve is a **relationship, not an effect**. The settings live on the *bed* —
the track that gets processed — and name the voices to listen to, exactly as a
sidechain compressor does. Never put a carve on a voice track.

`strength` derives six numbers that move together in any real mix: how deep to
cut, how many bands, how wide, how far to favour intelligibility over raw voice
energy, how far the level may drop, and how far under the voice to aim.

| Strength | Result |
| - | - |
| `0` | Spectral only — one band, no level match at all |
| `0.25` (default) | A 6 dB dip in three bands with 6 dB of level room |
| `0.5` | The dip reaches 10 dB — where a carve starts being heard as an effect |
| Above `0.5` | Deliberate territory for a loud bed under a quiet voice |

Every value becomes an envelope of the speech's own level: silence leaves the bed
alone, a loud passage pushes the carve to full depth. There is no static mode.

Inside a carved bed the signal runs through the dips first, then the level match,
then anything you built yourself — which is why a limiter you add still acts as
the last ceiling.

Voices are summed onto the bed's clock before anything is measured, so one
analysis covers all of them. Voices that never play while the bed does are left
out; they cannot mask it.

**Name a group, not a run of clip ids.** A list of ids has to be exhaustively
right and stays right only until the next edit — a fourth narration clip added
later plays outside the carve's awareness and the bed silently fails to duck
under it. A `sources` list naming two or more plain clip ids is reported as
`audio_carve_ungrouped_sources`.

There are two arrangements where naming the group is **worse** than naming ids,
and both come from the group form resolving later and wider than the analysis
that wrote it:

| Arrangement | What would happen |
| - | - |
| The bed is itself a member of the voice group | The bed is handed to itself as a voice and carved against its own content |
| The group also holds a member classified music or SFX | That member enters the sidechain on a later analysis, ducking the bed under a whoosh |

Neither shows up on the run that writes it — the analysis sums the voices it
detected, so the first pass is correct however wrong the stored attribute is. It
surfaces on the next re-analysis, against a file the previous run declared good.
Keep the bed in its own group.

What a carve writes is an ordinary chain of `peaking` filters plus a `gain`
stage, tagged `fromCarve`, and one automation lane per carved parameter. That
tagging is the whole trick: a re-run replaces the previous carve and leaves every
effect and lane you built by hand exactly where it was.

### From the command line

The script ships with the `media-use` skill; `<SKILL_DIR>` is that skill's folder.

```bash theme={null}
node <SKILL_DIR>/audio/scripts/carve.mjs --comp index.html
```

That is the whole command — it finds the voice and the bed itself and prints what
it decided:

```text theme={null}
bed    music-bed (name looks like music)
voice  narration (only track left)
carve  strength 0.25
bands  400Hz -6dB q1.4, 1000Hz -3dB q1.4, 1600Hz -3.17dB q1.4
level  216-point envelope, floor -6 dB
```

Name tracks with `--bed` / `--voice` (repeatable) when the automatic choice is
wrong, `--strength` to push it, `--dry-run` to see the report and write nothing.
It refuses when it cannot tell which track is the bed rather than carving the
wrong one.

**What it records in `sources`.** When every voice it analysed shares exactly one
group, and that group is safe to name, it writes the group id. It falls back to
the individual clip ids — and says so — when the group contains the bed or a
member classified music or SFX, for the reasons in the table above. A group
member classified voice or unknown that this run did not analyse is *not* a
reason to fall back: picking up a clip that starts playing later is the whole
point of naming the group.

Track choice is by name first, using the same classifier the browser editor's picker uses, so
the two cannot disagree: an id or filename that looks like music (`music`, `bgm`,
`bed`, `score`…) is the bed, and everything else playing over it that is not
SFX-shaped is a voice. Needs `ffmpeg` on `PATH` and `@hyperframes/core`
installed in the project.

## Groups and mute

A group sums its members through one bus, and the bus carries the group's own
volume, FX chain, and automation. In the render each group is sub-mixed into a
single track at full composition length before entering the main mix, so a
group-level effect hears the sum rather than each member separately.

| Control | Where it lives | Reaches the export |
| - | - | - |
| Mute | `data-hidden` on the group element or the clip | **Yes** — muted members are dropped from the rendered mix |

## Preview and render

Both read the same two attributes through the same builders, which is why
preview predicts the render:

| | Preview | Render |
| - | - | - |
| Context | Live `AudioContext` | `OfflineAudioContext` in the headless browser |
| Unreadable chain | Plays **dry**, so the composition stays workable | **Fails the whole mix** |
| Volume lane | Scheduled on the graph | Baked into the PCM by the mixer |
| Editing an attribute mid-playback | Picked up by a `MutationObserver` | n/a |

Effects with a tail — `reverb`, `delay` — make the rendered track **longer** than
its source, and the mix is told how much. A bed with reverb therefore no longer
ends exactly at its `data-duration`. That is expected.

## What the linter checks

Almost no static gate covers a mix. Four rules exist:

| Rule | Reports |
| - | - |
| `audio_attribute_unreadable` | A `data-automation` or `data-fx-chain` the render cannot parse: not JSON, no `"version": 1`, no `lanes` / `nodes` array, a lane without `target` or `points`, a node without `type`. The render fails on it, locally and in the cloud |
| `audio_carve_ungrouped_sources` | A carve naming two or more plain clip ids instead of a group |
| `audio_volume_double_automation` | A `volume` lane on a track that also has a GSAP tween on `volume` — the lane wins, the tween is ignored |
| `audio_volume_tween_overrides_gain` | An authored `data-volume` on a track whose `volume` is tweened — the tween's values are absolute and replace that gain rather than scaling it |

Nothing checks a lane's target or an effect's type and parameters. What enforces
those is the render. Beyond that, a mix is verified by rendering and listening.


# Color grading implementation
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/reference/color-grading

Persist, automate, animate, and spatially isolate media color grading.

Use this reference when browser editor controls are not enough: you need to write a
grade into HTML, apply it from automation, animate a supported property, or
limit an effect to a composited region. For visual correction and everyday
browser editor use, start with [Color grading](/guides/media-effects#fix-and-grade-the-color).

## Persist a grade

The browser editor and the CLI store the resolved grade in `data-color-grading`:

```html theme={null}
<video
  id="interview"
  src="./assets/interview.mp4"
  data-color-grading='{"preset":"skin-soft","intensity":0.7}'
></video>
```

Apply the same validated payload from the CLI:

```bash theme={null}
npx hyperframes media-treatment \
  --selector '#interview' \
  --grading '{"preset":"skin-soft","intensity":0.7}' \
  --apply
```

Add `--dry-run --json` to inspect the change without writing it. Use `--clear`
to remove the treatment.

## Grade a whole lane

A camera cut into hundreds of clips takes one grade, set once. Put the grade
on an `<hf-color-group>` and point each clip at it with `data-color-group`:

```html theme={null}
<hf-color-group
  id="tamer-cam"
  data-label="Tamer"
  data-color-grading='{"preset":"skin-soft","intensity":0.7}'
></hf-color-group>

<video id="tamer-01" data-color-group="tamer-cam" src="./assets/tamer.mp4" …></video>
<video id="tamer-02" data-color-group="tamer-cam" src="./assets/tamer.mp4" …></video>
<video
  id="tamer-03"
  data-color-group="tamer-cam"
  data-color-grading='{"adjust":{"exposure":0.3}}'
  src="./assets/tamer.mp4"
  …
></video>
```

* `data-color-grading` on the group takes the same JSON as on a clip. Editing it
  regrades every member, in preview and in render.
* `data-color-group` goes on the `<video>`, `<img>` or `<canvas>`. Membership is
  held by the member, so a deleted clip simply leaves the group.
* **A clip's own `data-color-grading` wins.** It replaces the group's grade for
  that clip, so `tamer-03` above gets only its exposure lift, not skin-soft.
* `data-color-group=""` is no group, and a group id with no `<hf-color-group>`
  element leaves the clip ungraded. Removing the element, or its
  `data-color-grading`, ungrades its members.
* Groups do not nest. Group ids share the element-id namespace.
* The element is inert: the runtime injects
  `hf-color-group{display:contents!important}`. Close it with
  `</hf-color-group>`, since HTML ignores `/>` on a custom element.

## Animate a supported property

Nine grading properties expose CSS custom properties that a paused timeline
can tween directly:

```text theme={null}
--hf-color-grading-ascii
--hf-color-grading-bloom
--hf-color-grading-blur
--hf-color-grading-dither
--hf-color-grading-exposure
--hf-color-grading-intensity
--hf-color-grading-kuwahara
--hf-color-grading-pixelate
--hf-color-grading-lut-intensity
```

Once set, a property overrides the payload's value for that control, whether it
comes from the element's inline style, a stylesheet or a parent. Set it only on
media you animate, starting at the value the tween begins from; leave it unset
for a static grade. Then animate it on the registered timeline:

```js theme={null}
tl.to(
  "#plate",
  {
    "--hf-color-grading-pixelate": 0.5,
    duration: 3,
    ease: "power2.inOut",
  },
  0.3,
);
```

`--hf-color-grading-intensity` scales the primary correction, wheels, curves,
selections, and LUT. It is not a master control for detail and effect families
such as grain, halftone, bloom, tape, or CRT. Animate the specific exposed
property and verify that it moves before relying on it.

## Limit a grade to part of the frame

Grading selects pixels by value, not position. To treat one region, isolate it
as its own media layer:

| Result | Layer stack |
| - | - |
| Grade the subject only | Clean original plate, then a graded subject cutout |
| Grade the background only | Graded original plate, then a clean subject cutout |
| Grade one region of the subject | Clean cutout, then a second graded cutout clipped to the region |

```html theme={null}
<video
  src="media/room.mp4"
  muted
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="4"
  data-track-index="2"
></video>
<video
  src="media/subject.webm"
  muted
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="4"
  data-track-index="3"
></video>
<video
  src="media/subject.webm"
  muted
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="4"
  data-track-index="4"
  style="clip-path: ellipse(9.8% 15.5% at 50.7% 14.5%)"
  data-color-grading='{"intensity":1,"effects":{"pixelate":0.5}}'
></video>
```

Use the original clip as the background plate. A subject-removed plate leaves a
hole and can create a dark edge beneath a feathered cutout. A fixed `clip-path`
works only when the subject barely moves; real movement needs a tracked matte
produced outside HyperFrames.


# HTML schema reference
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/reference/html-schema

The current contract for a HyperFrames composition.

HyperFrames uses normal HTML and CSS for appearance. A small set of attributes
declares the frame size, duration, clips, media, and nested compositions.

For a gentler explanation, start with [Compositions](/concepts/compositions) and
[Data attributes](/concepts/data-attributes).

## Minimal composition

```html theme={null}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=1920, height=1080" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      body { margin: 0; }
      #root {
        position: relative;
        width: 1920px;
        height: 1080px;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      .clip {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        display: grid;
        place-items: center;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div
      id="root"
      data-composition-id="main"
      data-start="0"
      data-duration="5"
      data-width="1920"
      data-height="1080"
    >
      <section
        id="title-card"
        class="clip"
        data-start="0"
        data-duration="5"
        data-track-index="1"
      >
        <h1 id="title">Hello HyperFrames</h1>
      </section>
    </div>

    <script>
      window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
      const timeline = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
      timeline.fromTo(
        "#title",
        { y: 48, opacity: 0 },
        { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: "power3.out" },
        0.2,
      );
      window.__timelines.main = timeline;
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

The root is a real, explicitly sized box. Its `data-composition-id` matches the
timeline registry key.

## Composition root

| Attribute | Required | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `data-composition-id` | Yes | Unique composition ID |
| `data-start="0"` | Yes on the top-level root | Start of the composition |
| `data-width` and `data-height` | Yes | Authored frame dimensions in pixels |
| `data-duration` | Usually | Total render duration in seconds |
| `data-no-timeline` | Only for a timeline-free composition | Tells the runtime not to wait for a timeline. Without it a composition that never registers one still waits out `player-ready-timeout` (45 s by default) on every render; `hyperframes lint` reports this as `missing_data_no_timeline` |

An explicit root `data-duration` is the render length. The compiler reads it
before composition scripts run, so a script or variable override cannot change
that value for the same render.

The root may omit `data-duration` only when HyperFrames can infer a finite
duration from the registered animation runtime or timed media. Three.js,
unbounded animation, and timeline-free compositions need an explicit duration.

## Timed clips

| Attribute | Required | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `id` | Yes | Stable identifier for timing, editing, and animation |
| `data-start` | Yes | Start in seconds or a relative timing expression |
| `data-duration` | Yes for DOM and nested-composition clips; optional for image (3 s default), video and audio (source length) | Visible slot length in seconds |
| `data-track-index` | No | browser editor timeline lane, display only. The render never reads it and it does not prevent overlap |
| `class="clip"` | Recommended for authored timed DOM and image elements | Layout and tooling convention. Visibility is keyed off `data-start`, but the shared `.clip` rule supplies the full-frame box |

`data-track-index` does not control paint order. Use CSS `z-index` for
front-to-back layering. Two clips on the same track may overlap in time; the
lane is a browser editor display row, not a scheduling constraint.

Negative `z-index` values are valid CSS, but an opaque ancestor background can
cover the clip if its parent does not create a stacking context. Add
`isolation: isolate` to that parent to keep the negative layer above the
parent's background and below its foreground siblings. See the
[before/after example](/concepts/data-attributes#keep-negative-layers-inside-their-parent).
The `negative_z_index` lint warning also fires on isolated layers because it
checks CSS text rather than computed stacking contexts.

Video visibility is managed as media and does not require `class="clip"`.
Audio has no visual lifecycle.

## Media

```html theme={null}
<video
  id="demo"
  src="./assets/demo.mp4"
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="8"
  data-track-index="0"
  muted
  playsinline
></video>
```

| Attribute | Applies to | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `data-media-start` / `data-playback-start` | Video, audio, nested composition | Offset into the source file, used by trim and split. Two groups of readers disagree, so the right name depends on the element. **Read only `data-media-start`:** the timing compiler, the HTML parser, `hyperframes validate` (which only inspects `<audio>`), and the engine's audio mixer (which feeds ffmpeg `-ss`). **Read `data-playback-start` first, falling back to `data-media-start`:** the runtime player, the browser editor (which also writes it), and `hyperframes snapshot`. Because the audio mixer reads only `data-media-start`, a `<video>` authored with just `data-playback-start` renders a trimmed picture over untrimmed audio. Set the name by kind: **`<video>` / `<audio>` → `data-media-start`**; **nested composition → `data-playback-start`** — composition hosts are inspected only by the playback-start-first readers (the media-start-only ones are all `<video>`/`<audio>`-scoped). `data-media-start` still works there as a fallback, but `data-playback-start` is the canonical name the browser editor writes and normalises to for new composition hosts, so the other name works until an edit rewrites it (it is the [child-timeline offset](/concepts/compositions)). |
| `data-playback-rate` | Video, audio, nested composition | Playback multiplier from `0.1` to `10`. A `rate` lane in `data-automation` overrides it; see [Speed ramps](/reference/speed-ramps) |
| `data-volume` | Video and audio | Static gain. `1` is 0 dB, `0` is silence, and values above `1` boost up to `3.98` (+12 dB). Multiplies any volume lane, and on a clip it applies ahead of the clip's audio effects |
| `data-fade-in` / `data-fade-out` | Video and audio | Clip-edge fades in seconds: gain rises 0 → 1 over the first `data-fade-in` seconds and falls 1 → 0 over the last `data-fade-out` seconds of the clip. Linear, anchored to the clip's own edges (a fade-out follows a later trim), and multiplied on top of `data-volume` and any volume lane. Fades that together exceed the clip are scaled to meet inside it. The browser editor drags them from the dots at an audio clip's top corners or types them in the inspector's Fade rows |
| `data-has-audio="true"` | Video | Declares that the video contributes audio |

Video and audio may omit `data-duration` when their intrinsic duration is known
and the whole remaining source should play.

Do not imperatively call `play()`, `pause()`, or set `currentTime`.
HyperFrames owns media playback and seeking. A `<video>` with sound declares `data-has-audio="true"` and is not muted. Silent footage is `muted`. Every timed `<video>` must say one or the other (lint `video_missing_muted`).

Media can live inside nested composition markup. Keep element IDs unique across
the assembled project because render-time frame injection targets those IDs.

## Color grading and media effects

The browser editor and the CLI store color correction, grading, finishing controls, LUTs,
and media effects on an image or video with `data-color-grading`:

```html theme={null}
<video
  id="demo"
  src="./assets/demo.mp4"
  data-color-grading='{
    "preset": "clean-studio",
    "intensity": 0.8,
    "adjust": { "highlights": -0.08, "shadows": 0.06 },
    "details": { "grain": 0.12, "vignette": 0.08 },
    "effects": { "bloom": 0.12 },
    "colorSpace": "rec709"
  }'
></video>
```

The current effect families include essentials, retro and glitch, print, and
art treatments. Run
`npx hyperframes media-treatment --capabilities --json` for the current
machine-readable surface instead of hard-coding an old effect list.

The grading pipeline applies to real `<img>` and `<video>` elements. It does
not grade a complete HTML scene. Use the browser editor or
[`media-treatment`](/packages/cli#media-treatment) for normal authoring; see
[Color Grading](/guides/media-effects#fix-and-grade-the-color) and [Media Effects](/guides/media-effects)
for the workflow and current SDR/HDR boundary.

## Relative timing

A non-numeric `data-start` refers to the end of another clip in the same
composition:

```html theme={null}
<video
  id="intro"
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="4"
  data-track-index="0"
  src="./intro.mp4"
  muted
  playsinline
></video>

<section
  id="result"
  class="clip"
  data-start="intro + 0.5"
  data-duration="3"
  data-track-index="0"
>
  Result
</section>
```

Supported forms are `clip-id`, `clip-id + seconds`, and
`clip-id - seconds`. References stay within one composition, must resolve to a
known duration, and cannot form a cycle. Put intentional overlaps on different
tracks.

## Nested compositions

The host declares a fixed timeline window:

```html theme={null}
<div
  id="pricing-scene"
  data-composition-id="pricing"
  data-composition-src="./compositions/pricing.html"
  data-start="4"
  data-duration="6"
  data-track-index="1"
  data-width="1920"
  data-height="1080"
></div>
```

The host `data-composition-id` must match the ID inside the source file and its
timeline registry key. The host `data-duration` controls how long the nested
composition remains visible. A shorter inner timeline holds its final state;
a shorter host duration cuts the slot.

A nested composition file transports its live markup through `<template>`.
Styles and scripts needed by that composition must be inside the template:

```html theme={null}
<template>
  <style>
    #root {
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
    }
  </style>

  <div
    id="root"
    data-composition-id="pricing"
    data-width="1920"
    data-height="1080"
  >
    <!-- scene content -->
  </div>

  <script>
    window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
    const timeline = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
    // scene animation
    window.__timelines.pricing = timeline;
  </script>
</template>
```

HyperFrames seeks nested timelines independently. Do not add a child timeline
manually to the parent GSAP timeline.

## Variables

Declare the schema with `data-composition-variables`, then pass values through a
render or a nested host:

```html theme={null}
<html
  data-composition-variables='[
    {"id":"title","type":"string","label":"Title","default":"Hello"}
  ]'
>
```

```html theme={null}
<div
  data-composition-id="pricing"
  data-composition-src="./compositions/pricing.html"
  data-variable-values='{"title":"Built for teams"}'
  data-start="0"
  data-duration="6"
  data-track-index="1"
  data-width="1920"
  data-height="1080"
></div>
```

Use `data-var-text`, `data-var-src`, or CSS `var(--variableId)` for direct
bindings. Use `getVariables()` when the value affects logic.

## Animation contract

A composition using GSAP must:

* create one finite timeline with `{ paused: true }`;
* register it on `window.__timelines` after adding its tweens;
* use the same key as `data-composition-id`;
* avoid wall-clock state, unseeded randomness, and infinite repeats.

HyperFrames controls seeking. Composition code describes how the visual state
looks at a given time.

Asynchronous setup, such as [loading a font before measuring text](/guides/gsap-animation#load-fonts-before-measuring-text), is supported. Register the completed timeline at the end of the callback, after its tweens are added. Do not register an empty timeline before the asynchronous build finishes.

Every element with `data-composition-id` participates in timeline readiness.
For a static nested section, use an ordinary `id` instead, or add
`data-no-timeline` to declare that no timeline will be registered. Otherwise,
the renderer waits up to the player-ready timeout for that element's timeline.
`hyperframes lint` reports bare composition hosts that have neither a matching
timeline registration nor an explicit opt-out as `missing_data_no_timeline`.

## Validate

```bash theme={null}
npx hyperframes lint
npx hyperframes check
```

`lint` checks the static contract. `check` opens the project in a browser and
checks runtime behavior, layout, motion, and contrast. Watch representative
snapshots and the finished render as the final visual gate.


# Lint rules
Source: https://hyperframes.heygen.com/reference/lint-rules

Every lint finding code with its severity, what it catches, and how to fix it.

`hyperframes lint`, `hyperframes check` and the `@hyperframes/lint` package report findings with a stable code. This page lists every code with its severity, what it catches, and how to fix it. The codes come straight from the rule set in `packages/lint/src/rules/` plus the project-level probes that run as part of a project lint.

Severities:

* **Error** — the composition is broken or the render will fail or visibly diverge. Fails `hyperframes check` by default.
* **Warning** — a quality, determinism or maintainability hazard. Does not fail `hyperframes check` unless you pass `--strict`; in `render`, warnings abort only under `--strict-all`.
* **Info** — a heads-up that needs no action. Shown by `hyperframes lint --verbose`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Looking for a code from a render or check log? Codes appear in the output of `npx hyperframes lint [dir]` — add `--json` to script over them. `check` additionally runs runtime, layout and motion audits beyond these lint rules; see [Troubleshooting](/help).

## Structure and timeline

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/structure.ts`.

The five codes marked **Warning or error** are warnings when the CLI lints a project, and errors when the browser editor
lints the file it is editing.

### `nested_structure_needs_subcomposition`

**Warning or error.** A top-level timeline element contains another nested structure instead of a sub-composition mount. The timeline draws one row per top-level element, and the root composition is built only from sub-compositions.

**Fix:** Move the element and its contents into a sub-composition file and mount it with `data-composition-src`.

### `timeline_element_missing_timing`

**Warning or error.** A timeline element has no `data-duration`, so the timeline cannot draw where it ends.

**Fix:** Add `data-duration` (in seconds) to the element.

### `caption_track_kind_missing`

**Warning or error.** An element looks like a caption row but is not marked as one, so the timeline cannot group it on the caption track.

**Fix:** Add `data-track-kind="captions"` to the element.

### `multiple_caption_tracks`

**Warning or error.** Captions are spread across several timeline tracks instead of one caption lane.

**Fix:** Give every caption element the same `data-track-index`.

### `clip_ends_past_root_duration`

**Warning.** A clip runs past the root composition's `data-duration`, so it is cut off in previews, posters and renders.

**Fix:** Extend the root `data-duration`, or make the clip end at or before it.

### `nested_clip_never_visible`

**Warning or error.** A timed clip sits inside another timed element, and its time window never overlaps that
element's, so it never appears. A nested clip's `data-start` counts from the composition's start, not from the
element around it. Runs in sub-composition files too.

**Fix:** Give the clip a `data-start` inside its parent's window, in composition time, or move it out of the
parent.

## Composition contract

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/composition.ts`.

### `invalid_composition_variables_declaration`

**Error.** `data-composition-variables` is not valid JSON or not an array of variable declarations.

**Fix:** Provide a JSON array such as `data-composition-variables='[{"id":"title","type":"string","label":"Title","default":"Hello"}]'` — single-quote the attribute, double-quote the JSON.

### `invalid_variable_values_json`

**Error.** `data-variable-values` is not valid JSON.

**Fix:** Single-quote the attribute and double-quote the JSON keys and values, e.g. `data-variable-values='{"title":"Hello"}'`.

### `unknown_variable_binding`

**Warning.** An element binds a variable that is not declared in `data-composition-variables`, so the binding silently keeps the authored fallback.

**Fix:** Declare the variable on the composition root (`<html>`, or the `data-composition-id` root of a template or fragment composition).

### `unloadable_media_variable_default`

**Error.** A variable's default is a URL the runtime refuses to load, so bound elements render their authored fallback src while the render still exits 0.

**Fix:** Use a relative path, `http(s)`, `blob:`, or a `data:image/*` URI. Copy the file into the project and reference it relatively.

### `deprecated_data_end`

**Error.** A legacy `data-end` is used without `data-duration`, or a stale `data-end` disagrees with the `data-duration` next to it.

**Fix:** Replace `data-end` with `data-duration`. The compiler generates `data-end` from `data-duration` automatically.

### `deprecated_data_layer`

**Error.** The legacy `data-layer` attribute is used.

**Fix:** Replace it with `data-track-index`, the canonical name the browser editor and the linter read.

### `duplicate_composition_id`

**Error.** The same `data-composition-id` appears on several elements in one file — often a `<meta>` tag carrying the same id as the root `<div>`.

**Fix:** Keep `data-composition-id` on exactly one element: the composition root. Remove it from metadata or duplicate hosts.

### `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path`

**Error.** Asset paths use `../` to traverse above the project root; render and preview clamp or misresolve them.

**Fix:** Point the path at a file inside the project — from `compositions/scene.html`, both `../assets/x.png` and `assets/x.png` reach the project's `assets` folder.

### `composition_exceeds_inspection_viewport_cap`

**Warning.** The composition is larger than the 4096px viewport cap that `check`, `validate`, `snapshot`, `compare` and layout audits clamp to. `render` is unaffected, but a clean inspection result no longer covers the whole canvas.

**Fix:** Keep the authored size if the output needs it, and verify the region past the cap from a render rather than from inspection commands.

### `composition_file_too_large`

**Warning.** The HTML composition file has grown past a size where it stays easy to read, iterate on, and diff.

**Fix:** Split it into sub-compositions and mount them from the parent with `data-composition-src`.

### `composition_heavy_overlay_count_high`

**Warning.** Many elements carry heavy overlay CSS (`filter: blur`, `radial-gradient`, `clip-path`), which can cap capture performance — including hidden ones.

**Fix:** Split the composition and concat the pieces so each capture sees a small subset of heavy overlays; remove overlays that are not visible anyway.

### `missing_data_no_timeline`

**Warning.** A `data-composition-id` element (or the root) has neither a matching `window.__timelines` registration nor `data-no-timeline`, so the producer polls up to 45 seconds before timing out.

**Fix:** Register the timeline, mount the composition with `data-composition-src`, or add `data-no-timeline` for genuinely static sections.

### `negative_z_index`

**Warning.** `z-index` below 0 paints the element behind its nearest stacking context's content; with no stacking-context ancestor that is the composition root, so an opaque background there hides the element entirely.

**Fix:** Give the element's parent a stacking context (`isolation: isolate` is the cheapest; `transform`, `filter`, `opacity` below 1, `contain: paint`, `will-change` also work).

### `requestanimationframe_in_composition`

**Error.** `requestAnimationFrame` runs on wall-clock time, not the GSAP timeline, so it desyncs from frame capture and can flicker or drop frames in renders.

**Fix:** Use GSAP tweens or timeline `onUpdate` callbacks for animation logic instead.

### `root_composition_duration_derived`

**Warning.** The root has no `data-duration` and no GSAP timeline, so its length is inferred from its clips.

**Fix:** Add `data-duration="<seconds>"` to the root element to set the length yourself.

### `root_composition_missing_duration_source`

**Error.** The root has no `data-duration`, no GSAP timeline, and no CSS, WAAPI, Lottie or Three.js animation to infer a duration from, so the render engine cannot determine how long to capture and fails.

**Fix:** Add `data-duration="<seconds>"` to the root, or add a paused GSAP timeline registered on `window.__timelines`.

### `root_composition_missing_html_wrapper`

**Error.** An `index.html` carrying `data-composition-id` is a bare fragment without `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html>` or `<body>`, so browsers quirks-mode it and the preview server mis-serves it.

**Fix:** Wrap the composition in `<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="UTF-8"></head><body>...</body></html>`.

### `root_zoom_rescales_a_fixed_canvas`

**Error.** CSS `zoom` on the canvas rescales the painted composition inside a capture frame that does not rescale with it — the frame is sized from the root's `data-width` and `data-height` in layout pixels.

**Fix:** Author at the real size: set `data-width` and `data-height` (and the root's width and height) and drop the canvas-level `zoom`. To scale the output without changing layout, pass `--output-resolution` to render. `zoom` on descendants is fine.

### `split_data_attribute_selector`

**Error.** A CSS selector combines two attributes inside one `[...]` block, which browsers reject — GSAP timelines or `querySelector` calls fail before they register.

**Fix:** Use separate attribute selectors: `[data-composition-id="x"][data-track-index="1"]`.

### `standalone_composition_wrapped_in_template`

**Error.** The root `index.html` is wrapped in a `<template>` tag, so the runtime cannot play it — only sub-compositions loaded via `data-composition-src` use `<template>` wrappers.

**Fix:** Remove the `<template>` wrapper and serve the composition as a real document.

### `subcomposition_blanks_before_host`

**Warning.** A mounted sub-composition is blank for part of its host's window because its own `data-duration` is shorter than the slot it fills.

**Fix:** Set the sub-composition's `data-duration` to fill the host window, or cover the gap with another clip.

### `subcomposition_linked_style_names_root_id`

**Warning.** A stylesheet linked from a sub-composition has a rule on `#<root id>`, the id of the sub-composition's root. When the composition is compiled the root is merged into its host, so that selector matches nothing. The same rule in an inline `<style>` is rewritten and works.

**Fix:** Move the rule into a `<style>` inside the `<template>`, or select a child element of the root in the linked file instead of the root itself.

### `subcomposition_root_styled_by_class`

**Error.** A sub-composition's root element is styled through class selectors, but at render every rule is scoped to `[data-composition-id=...]`, so the class-keyed styles stop applying.

**Fix:** Give the root `id="root"` and style it with `#root` plus plain descendant selectors.

### `subcomposition_style_outside_template`

**Warning.** A sub-composition file with a `<template>` has a `<style>`, or a `<link rel="stylesheet">`
outside `<head>`, that sits outside the template. Mounting keeps only the template's content and the
stylesheet links in `<head>`, so those styles never apply in preview, snapshot or render.

**Fix:** Move it inside `<template>`, next to the composition root.

### `template_literal_selector`

**Error.** `querySelector` is called with a template-literal variable, which the bundler's CSS parser crashes on.

**Fix:** Use hardcoded string selectors instead of interpolated ones.

### `timed_element_missing_clip_class`

**Warning.** An element has timing attributes but no `class="clip"`. The runtime still times it, but the browser editor and the clip-ownership rules use `.clip` to recognise it, so it is harder to edit and to lint.

**Fix:** Add `class="clip"` to the element.

### `timeline_track_too_dense`

**Warning.** One track in this file carries more than 3 timed elements (audio, video, caption cues and sub-composition mounts are not counted), which makes the timeline harder to read, iterate on, and diff.

**Fix:** Split the elements into sub-compositions and mount them from the parent with `data-composition-src`.

## Document, CSS and scripts

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/core.ts`.

### `host_missing_composition_id`

**Error.** A `data-composition-src` host element has no `data-composition-id` of its own.

**Fix:** Set `data-composition-id` on every `data-composition-src` host element.

### `css_parse_error`

**Error.** A `<style>` block fails to parse as CSS.

**Fix:** Fix the reported CSS syntax error.

### `css_transition_used`

**Warning.** A CSS `transition` declaration runs on the browser clock and cannot be seeked deterministically across render workers. `transition: none` and all-zero durations are allowed.

**Fix:** Keep the class or attribute swap for state, but put the visual change on the paused GSAP timeline.

### `id_override_reduced_specificity`

**Warning.** A selector sets position properties through `[id=...]` or `:where(#id)`, which has class-level or zero specificity, so a compound class rule on the same element can silently win.

**Fix:** Use the plain `#id` selector; id specificity beats any selector built only from classes.

### `id_requires_css_escape`

**Error / warning.** An id starts with a digit, so `#id` selectors throw a `SyntaxError` in `querySelector` and GSAP, and CSS drops the rule. Error when such a selector is actually used in the composition, warning otherwise.

**Fix:** Rename the id to start with a letter (recommended), or build selectors with `CSS.escape(id)` at runtime.

### `inline_style_attribute_selector`

**Error.** A selector reads the inline `style` attribute (`[style]`, `[style*=...]` and the other forms).
GSAP writes inline styles every frame, and each write then restyles far more than the animated element.
The preview slows to a crawl.

**Fix:** Let the runtime hide hidden clips; it already hides their contents.
For a state of your own, toggle a class or data attribute from your script and select on that.

### `invalid_inline_script_syntax`

**Error.** An inline `<script>` is closed with malformed syntax.

**Fix:** Close inline scripts with a valid `</script>` tag.

### `missing_timeline_registry`

**Error.** The composition registers no `window.__timelines` registry at all.

**Fix:** Register each composition timeline on `window.__timelines[compositionId]`.

### `non_deterministic_code`

**Error.** A script uses a non-deterministic value source (`Math.random`, `Date.now`, `gsap.utils.random`, `"random(...)"`), so renders can differ between frames or runs.

**Fix:** Precompute the value once at build time and pass a constant, or seed and freeze it.

### `repeated_id_descendant_selector`

**Error.** A selector requires an id to be nested inside another element with the same id. Ids must be unique, so the selector can never match.

**Fix:** Remove the duplicate ancestor: change `#x #x` to `#x`.

### `root_dimensions_mismatch`

**Warning.** The root's `data-width`/`data-height` were edited directly, but the scaffold's `html, body` CSS and `<meta viewport>` still hold the old resolution, and a stale `overflow: hidden` body visually clips the correctly-sized root.

**Fix:** Update the body CSS and viewport to match, or scaffold with `hyperframes init --resolution portrait`.

### `root_missing_composition_id`

**Error.** The root composition is missing `data-composition-id`.

**Fix:** Add a stable `data-composition-id` to the entry composition wrapper.

### `root_missing_dimensions`

**Error.** The root composition is missing `data-width` or `data-height`.

**Fix:** Set numeric `data-width` and `data-height` on the entry composition root.

### `runtime_hidden_style_opacity`

**Error.** A selector observes the runtime-owned hidden style (used to hide native video during frame copying) and forces `opacity` to zero, which breaks the video replacement pipeline.

**Fix:** Remove the rule; the runtime already hides a hidden clip and its contents.
To fade or hide something yourself, animate it on the timeline, or toggle a class or data attribute and select on that.

### `scoped_css_missing_wrapper`

**Warning.** Scoped CSS targets a composition id for which no matching wrapper exists in this HTML.

**Fix:** Keep the matching composition wrapper, or align the CSS scope to an existing wrapper.

### `studio_missing_editable_id`

**Warning.** A timeline-visible element has no `id`, so the browser editor cannot target it stably for timeline and canvas edits.

**Fix:** Add a stable, human-readable id such as `id="hero-title"` to elements that agents or the browser editor should edit.

### `timeline_id_mismatch`

**Error.** A timeline is registered under a key for which no element carries the matching `data-composition-id`, so the runtime cannot auto-nest it.

**Fix:** Make `window.__timelines["<key>"]` match the element's `data-composition-id`, or vice versa.

### `unbalanced_style_tags`

**Error.** A `<style>` block is never closed (following markup is parsed as CSS and disappears), or an extra `</style>` closes the stylesheet early and dumps CSS into the body as visible text.

**Fix:** Keep `<style>` and `</style>` paired.

### `unclosed_tag_swallowed_element`

**Error.** A tag is missing its closing `>` before the next `<`, so the following element is swallowed as bogus attribute text and never becomes a real node.

**Fix:** Close the previous tag's `>` before opening the next element.

### `visible_markup_comment`

**Error.** CSS or JS block-comment syntax (`/* ... */`) appears in visible HTML markup, where only `<!-- ... -->` is a comment — so it renders as on-screen text.

**Fix:** Remove the text or convert it to a real HTML comment; keep CSS comments inside `<style>` and JS comments inside `<script>`.

## GSAP animation

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/gsap.ts`.

### `audio_reactive_single_tween_per_group`

**Warning.** Audio-reactive captions use a single tween per group based on peak values, which sets one static value and is not perceptible as audio reactivity.

**Fix:** Sample the audio data at 100-200ms intervals across each group's lifetime and create a tween per sample point.

### `gsap_animates_clip_element`

**Error.** GSAP sets visibility-affecting properties (`opacity`, `visibility`, `autoAlpha`) directly on a clip element whose visibility the framework owns.

**Fix:** Remove the visibility or autoAlpha tween, or move the content into a child `<div>` and target that instead.

### `gsap_callback_dom_measurement`

**Warning.** A timeline callback reaches DOM measurement (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getTotalLength`, `getComputedStyle`, ...). Callbacks re-fire on every seek, and a cold render worker runs them against a different layout than the sequential pass.

**Fix:** Do all measurement and DOM setup synchronously at build time, before registering the timeline, or derive geometry from fixed composition coordinates.

### `gsap_cold_seek_hidden_fromto_missing_reveal`

**Error.** An element authored hidden uses `gsap.fromTo()` whose destination vars omit `opacity`/`autoAlpha`, so cold render workers restore the hidden state and the element can stay invisible.

**Fix:** Add `opacity: 1` (or `autoAlpha: 1`) to the destination vars so every seek path establishes the visible end state.

### `gsap_css_transform_conflict`

**Error.** An element has a CSS `transform` (for example `translateX(-50%)` centering) and a GSAP tween animates transform properties — GSAP overwrites the full CSS transform.

**Fix:** Remove the transform from CSS and express it in GSAP properties instead; `tl.fromTo` with explicit start values is exempt.

### `gsap_from_opacity_noop`

**Error.** An element has CSS `opacity: 0` and a `gsap.from()` that also sets opacity to 0, so it animates from 0 to 0 and never appears.

**Fix:** Remove `opacity: 0` from the CSS or inline style and let the `gsap.from()` own the initial hidden state.

### `gsap_fullscreen_overlay_starts_visible`

**Error.** A full-frame overlay starts visible before its first GSAP opacity tween, so it covers earlier render frames — often as a blank or white video.

**Fix:** Author the overlay hidden in CSS, or add an immediate `gsap.set(..., { opacity: 0 })` before the reveal tween.

### `gsap_function_value_hazard`

**Error / warning.** A function-valued tween var reads transform-sensitive geometry, measures layout at tween init, or accesses its first parameter (which is a number, not the element). Error for transform-sensitive reads and bad member access, warning otherwise.

**Fix:** Compute the value once at build time and pass a constant; for per-element logic use the second parameter: `(index, target) => ...`.

### `gsap_group_selector_keyframes`

**Warning.** A GSAP tween targets several elements with shared keyframes, so editing one element's keyframes in the browser editor changes all of them.

**Fix:** Replace the group selector with individual `tl.to()` calls per element.

### `gsap_infinite_repeat`

**Error / warning.** A GSAP tween or timeline uses `repeat: -1`. Warning when the composition declares a finite `data-duration` (seeking and export are clipped to it), error when nothing bounds the timeline.

**Fix:** Declare a finite `data-duration`, or replace `repeat: -1` with a finite count such as `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(totalDuration / cycleDuration) - 1)`.

### `gsap_non_transform_motion`

**Error.** A GSAP tween animates layout properties (`left`, `top`, `width`, ...), text-reflow properties (`fontSize`, `letterSpacing`, ...) or sets `roundProps`, all of which snap to integer device pixels and stutter under frame capture.

**Fix:** Animate transforms instead: positional properties become `x`/`y`/`scale`; reflow properties need per-character splits or a static final value; remove `roundProps`.

### `gsap_relative_value_second_writer`

**Error.** A relative tween value (`+=...`) starts while another writer is still active on the same property, so different seek paths init the relative tween from different bases and the frame snaps.

**Fix:** Use absolute values or a `fromTo()` with explicit endpoints for that property. A relative value with a single writer is safe.

### `gsap_repeat_ceil_overshoot`

**Warning.** A repeat count computed with `Math.ceil` can overshoot the composition duration, extending the animation past it.

**Fix:** Use `Math.floor` in the repeat calculation: `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(totalDuration / cycleDuration) - 1)`.

### `gsap_repeat_floor_unclamped`

**Warning.** A repeat calculation can evaluate to `-1` when the composition is shorter than one cycle, which GSAP interprets as an infinite repeat.

**Fix:** Clamp the count at zero: `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(totalDuration / cycleDuration) - 1)`.

### `gsap_repeat_refresh_relative_value`

**Error.** `repeatRefresh: true` combined with a relative value accumulates per iteration; a cold render worker seeking into iteration N never performed the earlier accumulation, so its result differs.

**Fix:** Remove `repeatRefresh: true`, or replace the relative value with absolute endpoints (a `fromTo()`).

### `gsap_repeated_fromto_without_baseline`

**Warning.** Several `tl.fromTo()` calls target the same element with no stable baseline, so the last-authored "from" values become the resting state for any seek before the first tween runs.

**Fix:** Add `immediateRender: false` to every `fromTo` except the earliest-positioned one.

### `gsap_timeline_not_registered`

**Error.** A GSAP timeline is created but never registered on `window.__timelines`, so the runtime never discovers it and the animation does not play in preview or render.

**Fix:** Add `window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};` and assign the timeline under the composition's `data-composition-id`.

### `gsap_timeline_registered_before_async_build`

**Error.** `window.__timelines` is assigned before the timeline is built inside `document.fonts.ready`, so an empty timeline registers first and can nest empty in sub-compositions.

**Fix:** Move the `window.__timelines[id] = tl` assignment to the end of the async build callback, after the tweens are added.

### `gsap_timeline_return_used_as_tween`

**Error.** Code captures the return of `tl.to()`/`tl.from()`/`tl.set()` expecting the tween, but those methods return the timeline itself — so a later `kill()` or overwrite hits the whole timeline.

**Fix:** Put the group of tweens in a nested timeline (`gsap.timeline()` added with `tl.add(nested, 0)`) and kill that instead.

### `gsap_timeline_set_initial_hide`

**Warning.** The initial hidden state is set with `tl.set(..., 0)` inside the paused timeline; a zero-duration set at position 0 does not render while the playhead sits exactly at 0, so frame 0 shows the un-hidden state.

**Fix:** Use `gsap.set(...)` outside the timeline, or author the hidden state directly in CSS or attributes.

### `gsap_undefined_css_variable`

**Warning.** GSAP animates a `var(--...)` CSS variable that no static CSS or composition-variable declaration defines, so the computed color may become invalid or transparent.

**Fix:** Define the variable in CSS, declare it in `data-composition-variables`, or add a `var(--x, #fff)` fallback.

### `missing_gsap_plugin`

**Error.** A tween uses a plugin-specific property such as `motionPath`, but the plugin is not loaded and registered, so core GSAP ignores the property.

**Fix:** Load the plugin before the animation script and register it with `gsap.registerPlugin(...)`, or express the motion with core `x`/`y` tweens.

### `missing_gsap_script`

**Error.** The composition uses GSAP but no GSAP script is loaded, so the animation will not run.

**Fix:** Add the GSAP `<script>` tag before the animation script.

### `overlapping_gsap_tweens`

**Warning.** Two GSAP tweens overlap on the same target for the same properties, so the later one overwrites the earlier mid-flight.

**Fix:** Shorten the earlier tween, move the later one, or add `overwrite: "auto"`.

### `svg_drawon_css_dasharray_conflict`

**Error.** GSAP writes `strokeDasharray` on an element whose CSS declares a multi-component `stroke-dasharray`; GSAP merges dash lists per component, so the CSS gap survives and the draw-on breaks.

**Fix:** Remove the CSS `stroke-dasharray` (decorative dashes belong on a separate element), or set the full two-component value in GSAP.

### `svg_round_cap_hidden_dash`

**Warning.** A round or square capped path is hidden with dasharray = gap = `pathLength` and dashoffset = dash.

Chrome can leave a zero-length sliver at the path end there, and the cap paints it as a dot on some curves.

**Fix:** Make the gap longer than the path (`stroke-dasharray="100 120"`, `stroke-dashoffset="110"`).

Or keep the element `visibility: hidden` until its draw tween starts.

### `svg_measure_before_path_d`

**Error / warning.** `getTotalLength()` is called on a path with no static `d` attribute, so it returns 0 and the dash animation dies. Error when no `d` assignment exists anywhere, warning when `d` is only assigned inside a function body.

**Fix:** Assign the path's `d` synchronously at build time (top level, before measuring), or author a static `d` attribute in the HTML.

## Media elements

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/media.ts`.

### `audio_attribute_unreadable`

**Error.** A `data-automation` or `data-fx-chain` is not one the render can parse: not JSON, no `"version": 1`, no `lanes` / `nodes` array, a lane without `target` or `points`, or a node without `type`. The audio mix fails on it, locally and in the cloud.

**Fix:** Write it as `{"version": 1, "lanes": [...]}` (automation) or `{"version": 1, "nodes": [...]}` (effect chain), or remove the attribute.

### `audio_carve_ungrouped_sources`

**Warning.** A voiceover carve names its member clips directly instead of carving an `<hf-audio-group>`, so the list silently rots when clips change.

**Fix:** Group the voice clips and carve against the group.

### `audio_group_carve_attr`

**Warning.** An `<hf-audio-group>` carries `data-fx-carve` (or a carve-derived chain), but a carve belongs on the bed clip, not the bus.

**Fix:** Remove `data-fx-carve` from the group and carve the bed clip instead.

### `audio_group_holds_elements`

**Warning.** Elements sit inside an `<hf-audio-group>`. Most often the group was written self-closed (`<hf-audio-group id="sfx" />`), which HTML does not close on a custom element, so every later sibling lands inside it. Being inside routes no audio through the bus, and while the group has `data-hidden` those elements are hidden and silenced in preview and render.

**Fix:** Close the group with `</hf-audio-group>` right after its opening tag, and give clips meant for the bus `data-audio-group`.

### `audio_group_no_members`

**Error.** An audio group exists that no clip joins, so its fader, effects and automation are silently dropped.

**Fix:** Add `data-audio-group="<id>"` to the clips the bus is for, or delete the bus.

### `audio_group_timing_attrs`

**Warning.** An `<hf-audio-group>` carries timing attributes (`data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-track-index`). A group has no clip window of its own; its members carry the timing.

**Fix:** Remove the timing attributes from the group and set them on the member clips.

### `audio_volume_double_automation`

**Warning.** An element has both a volume automation lane and a GSAP tween on `volume`; the lane wins and the tween is ignored in preview and render.

**Fix:** Keep one: delete the lane to tween, or drop the tween and shape the level in the lane.

### `audio_volume_tween_overrides_gain`

**Warning.** An element has `data-volume` gain and a GSAP tween on `volume`; tween values are absolute and replace the gain rather than scale it.

**Fix:** Write tween targets as absolute gains that already include the gain, or reset `data-volume` to 1 and let the tween carry the level.

### `base64_media_prohibited`

**Error.** Inline base64 audio or video is present. Base64 media bloats file size and breaks rendering.

**Fix:** Use a relative path or HTTPS URL for the `src` — never embed media as base64.

### `color_grading_invalid_json`

**Error.** `data-color-grading` on a `<video>` or `<img>` starts with `{` or `[` but is not valid JSON, so the grade does not render.

**Fix:** Use valid JSON, for example `data-color-grading='{"preset":"skin-soft","intensity":0.6,"adjust":{"highlights":-0.08}}'` — single-quote the attribute, double-quote the JSON.

### `color_grading_invalid_structure`

**Error.** `data-color-grading` parses as JSON but breaks the grading contract — an unsupported key, a value of the wrong type, or a number out of range. The runtime silently ignores unknown keys, so a control can look applied in the HTML yet never render. One finding is reported per problem, naming the offending path.

**Fix:** Correct or remove the value the finding names, following the [Color grading](/reference/color-grading) reference.

### `color_grading_non_media`

**Error.** `data-color-grading` is set on an element other than `<video>`, `<img>`, `<canvas>` or
`<hf-color-group>`, such as a wrapper or an element with a CSS background. The shader runtime only grades
real `<video>`, `<img>` and `<canvas>` elements, plus the members of a
[grade group](/reference/color-grading#grade-a-whole-lane), so the attribute has no effect.

**Fix:** Move the attribute to the `<video>`, `<img>` or `<canvas>` element itself.

### `duplicate_media_discovery_risk`

**Warning.** Several matching media entries share the same source, start and duration, so the compiler can discover the same media twice.

**Fix:** Remove the duplicated media nodes so discovery sees one.

### `duplicate_media_id`

**Error.** A media `id` is defined on multiple elements, so preview and the producer can build different media graphs.

**Fix:** Give each media element a unique `id`.

### `imperative_media_control`

**Error.** An inline script controls managed media imperatively (`play`, `pause`, `currentTime`, ...). HyperFrames must own playback to keep preview, timeline and renders deterministic.

**Fix:** Express timing with `data-start`/`data-duration` and media offsets such as `data-media-start` instead.

### `media_crossorigin_breaks_preview`

**Error.** The element has `crossorigin`, which forces a CORS-checked fetch; if the host omits CORS headers, the load fails silently in the browser editor preview (blank media) while renders still work.

**Fix:** Remove `crossorigin` unless you read the media back through canvas, WebGL or WebAudio from a host known to send CORS headers.

### `media_missing_data_start`

**Error.** A media element has `src` but no `data-start`, so HyperFrames cannot own its playback and preview and render can diverge.

**Fix:** Add `data-start="0"` (or the intended start) and `data-duration` if the clip should stop before the source ends.

### `media_missing_id`

**Error.** A timed media element has no `id`, so the renderer cannot discover it — the audio goes silent or the video freezes.

**Fix:** Add a unique `id` attribute to the element.

### `media_missing_src`

**Error.** A timed media element has no `src` (on the element or a `<source>` child), so the renderer cannot load it.

**Fix:** Add `src` to the element, or a `<source src="...">` child.

### `media_preload_none`

**Warning.** The element has `preload="none"`, which prevents the renderer from loading the media (the compiler strips it for renders, but preview can misbehave).

**Fix:** Remove `preload="none"` or change it to `preload="auto"`.

### `media_runtime_src_mutation`

**Warning.** An inline script mutates the `src` of existing managed media, which races media discovery and extraction.

**Fix:** Author the final static `src`, or bind `data-var-src` to a declared variable so the source is applied before discovery.

### `media_src_kind_mismatch`

**Error.** A media URL's kind does not match its element — for example a still image on `<video>` or a video URL on `<img>`, so the element renders nothing.

**Fix:** Match the element to the media: `<img>` for stills, `<video>` for video URLs, `<audio>` for sound.

### `media_variable_src_no_fallback`

**Warning.** The element relies on `data-var-src` with no fallback `src`, so renders without that variable value cannot load the media, and audio extraction reads the authored `src`.

**Fix:** Add a fallback `src` the composition can render with when the variable is not provided.

### `nested_media_start_basis_ambiguous`

**Warning.** A nested media element's `data-start` is ambiguous: composition-local or a legacy root-global timestamp, and the two read as different frames.

**Fix:** Keep `data-start` composition-local, or mark the legacy basis with `data-hf-media-start-basis="global"`; otherwise convert to local time.

### `placeholder_media_url`

**Error.** The element uses a placeholder media URL that will 404 at render time.

**Fix:** Replace it with a real, reachable media URL.

### `self_closing_media_tag`

**Error.** A self-closing media tag (`<video ... />`) is invalid HTML: the browser leaves the tag open and swallows all subsequent elements as invisible fallback content, making the composition invisible.

**Fix:** Write explicit closing tags: `<video ...></video>`. Media elements must never be self-closed.

### `speed_ramp_on_non_media`

**Warning.** A speed-ramp lane sits on a non-media element; only `<video>` and `<audio>` clips can be retimed, so the lane does nothing.

**Fix:** Move the rate lane onto the video or audio clip, or retime an animation with a GSAP timeline.

### `video_audio_double_source`

**Error.** An `<audio>` element and a `<video>` element point at the same source at the same time; the unmuted video already carries the sound, so playback echoes.

**Fix:** Let the video carry its own sound (recommended), or mute the video and keep the separate `<audio>` when picture and sound must be cut independently.

### `video_missing_muted`

**Error.** A timed `<video>` declares neither `muted` nor `data-has-audio="true"`, so the linter cannot tell silent footage from sound-carrying footage.

**Fix:** Add `data-has-audio="true"` when the file has sound, or `muted` when it is silent.

### `video_muted_with_declared_audio`

**Error.** A `<video>` declares `data-has-audio="true"` but also carries `muted`, so the browser editor preview silences the audio the declaration promises.

**Fix:** Remove `muted` if the video should be audible, or drop `data-has-audio` and use `data-volume="0"` for silent visual video.

### `video_nested_in_timed_element`

**Error.** A `<video>` with `data-start` is nested inside another timed element; the frame extractor resolves the video's start without the wrapper's offset while visibility uses the wrapper's window, so the clip shows wrong frames and disappears partway.

**Fix:** Time the wrapper or the video, never both: remove `data-start` from the wrapper, or move the `<video>` up to be a direct child of the stage.

## Captions

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/captions.ts`.

### `caption_container_relative_position`

**Error.** A caption selector uses `position: relative`, which causes overflow and breaks caption stacking.

**Fix:** Use `position: absolute` for all caption elements.

### `caption_exit_missing_hard_kill`

**Error.** Caption exit animations (`tl.to` with `opacity: 0`) have no hard `tl.set` kill, so conflicting karaoke tweens can leave captions stuck on screen.

**Fix:** Add `tl.set(groupEl, { opacity: 0, visibility: "hidden" }, group.end)` after every exit tween as a deterministic kill.

### `caption_fittext_scale_mismatch`

**Warning.** `fitTextFontSize` uses a `maxWidth` that leaves no headroom for emphasis words scaled above 1x, so the effective width can overflow the composition.

**Fix:** Reduce `maxWidth` to leave headroom for the scale factor.

### `caption_overflow_clips_scaled_words`

**Error.** A caption container has `overflow: hidden` while GSAP scales caption words above 1x, so scaled emphasis words and their glow are clipped.

**Fix:** Use `overflow: visible` on caption containers and prevent overflow with `fitTextFontSize` and a reduced `maxWidth` instead.

### `caption_text_overflow_risk`

**Warning.** A caption selector has `white-space: nowrap` but no `max-width`, so long phrases clip off-screen.

**Fix:** Add `max-width: 1600px` (landscape) or `900px` (portrait), keeping overflow visible.

### `caption_textshadow_on_group_container`

**Warning.** `textShadow` is tweened on a caption group container; with semi-transparent children the glow renders as a visible rectangle behind the whole group.

**Fix:** Apply `textShadow` to individual active word elements and use scale on the group for pulsing.

### `caption_transcript_not_inline`

**Error.** A captions composition loads its transcript with `fetch()`, but the browser editor caption editor needs an inline `var TRANSCRIPT = [...]` array to detect and edit captions.

**Fix:** Embed the transcript inline as `var TRANSCRIPT = [...]` with JSON-quoted keys.

## Fonts

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/fonts.ts`.

### `font_family_without_font_face`

**Error.** A `@font-face`-undeclared font family is used, so the renderer cannot supply it and text falls back to a default face.

**Fix:** Declare each family with `@font-face` pointing at the captured `.woff2` files, or bundle the font under `capture/assets/fonts/`.

The declaration may use a quoted or unquoted family name. If `font-family` is the last descriptor in the block, its final semicolon is optional. Families named in a `font` shorthand (`font: 500 16px/1 "PingFang SC", sans-serif`) count the same as `font-family`.

### `font_face_local_only`

**Warning.** An `@font-face` names only `local()` sources. A local render draws the font installed on this machine; a cloud render, or another machine without it, falls back to a different font.

**Fix:** Add a `url()` source pointing at a `.woff2` file inside the project, or use a Google Fonts family.

### `system_font_will_alias`

**Warning.** A system font family is used without a matching `@font-face`; in distributed rendering system-font capture is disabled, so the font is substituted at render time and text can reflow. Only reported when the linter runs with the `distributed: true` option (linting for distributed or Lambda renders); a local render captures the system font as designed, so it is not flagged there.

**Fix:** Bundle the font with `@font-face` and a project-local file instead of relying on OS fonts.

## Textures

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/textures.ts`.

### `texture_class_missing_base`

**Warning.** A texture material class is used without the base `hf-texture-text` class, so the texture pipeline does not engage.

**Fix:** Add the base class alongside the material class, e.g. `class="hf-texture-text hf-texture-lava"`.

### `texture_class_unknown`

**Error.** A texture material class is not defined by any local CSS, so the text renders untextured.

**Fix:** Paste the Texture Mask Text component's `<style>` block into the composition, or fix the class typo.

### `texture_drop_shadow_on_text`

**Warning.** A drop shadow is applied directly to textured text, which shadows the mask rather than the glyphs.

**Fix:** Wrap the textured text and apply `filter: drop-shadow(...)` to the wrapper, not the `hf-texture-text` element.

### `texture_text_missing_mask`

**Warning.** `hf-texture-text` is used without a texture material class or a custom `mask-image`, so there is nothing to reveal.

**Fix:** Add a material class such as `hf-texture-lava`, or set `mask-image` and `-webkit-mask-image` on the element.

## Slideshows

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/slideshow.ts`.

### `slideshow_invalid`

**Error.** A slideshow island contains invalid JSON or a structure that does not match the manifest schema.

**Fix:** Make the `<script type="application/hyperframes-slideshow+json">` block valid JSON matching the SlideshowManifest schema.
If supplied, `startTime` and `endTime` must be finite JSON numbers. Quoted numbers such as `"0"`, `null`, and overflowing values such as `1e400` are invalid.

### `slideshow_unresolved_ref`

**Error.** The slideshow manifest references a `sceneId` with no matching scene element, or a scene with no explicit window.

**Fix:** Make every `sceneId` match a scene element's `data-composition-id`, or provide explicit `startTime`/`endTime`.

## Adapters: Lottie and Three.js

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/adapters.ts`.

### `missing_lottie_script`

**Error.** The composition uses Lottie but no Lottie script is loaded, so the animation will not render.

**Fix:** Add the `lottie-web` `<script>` tag before the Lottie code.

### `missing_three_script`

**Error.** The composition uses Three.js but no Three.js script is loaded, so the 3D scene will not render.

**Fix:** Add the Three.js `<script>` tag before the Three.js code.

## Linked clips

Source: `packages/lint/src/rules/linkedClips.ts`.

### `linked_clip_orphan`

**Warning.** A clip carries `data-link` whose partner clip no longer exists, so it edits as a group of one.

**Fix:** Remove the `data-link` attribute, or restore the partner clip.

### `linked_clips_out_of_sync`

**Warning.** Clips sharing a `data-link` differ in their timing attributes, but linked clips are edited as one.

**Fix:** Give every member the same `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-media-start` and `data-playback-rate`, or remove `data-link` from all of them to unlink.

## Project-level checks

Source: the project lint pass in `packages/lint/src/project.ts`, `packages/lint/src/hyperframeLinter.ts` and `packages/lint/src/hevcPreviewLint.ts`.

### `multiple_root_compositions`

**Error.** Several root-level HTML files carry `data-composition-id`, so the runtime may discover multiple entry points and duplicate audio playback.

**Fix:** Keep exactly one root `index.html` with `data-composition-id`; remove or rename the extra files.

### `blank_root_with_standalone_composition`

**Error.** The default `index.html` has no renderable content while another file holds a standalone timed composition, so default commands open an empty video.

**Fix:** Move the composition into `index.html`, or mount it with `data-composition-src`; if the separate file is intentional, render it explicitly.

### `missing_or_empty_sub_composition`

**Error.** A `data-composition-src` points at a folder, an empty file, or a missing file, so the mount is unusable and the render pre-flight rejects it.

**Fix:** Point `data-composition-src` at the HTML file (such as `<folder>/index.html`) and make sure it renders content.

### `missing_local_asset`

**Error.** An element references local files that do not exist in the project, so the renderer silently skips them and the video ships with missing visuals.

**Fix:** Add the file to the project directory, or update the `src` to an existing file. A common cause is renamed captured assets.

### `audio_file_without_element`

**Warning.** The project contains audio files but no `<audio>` element in any composition, so the rendered video will be silent.

**Fix:** Add an `<audio>` element referencing the file.

### `audio_src_not_found`

**Error.** An `<audio>` element references files that are not in the project, so the rendered video will be silent.

**Fix:** Add the missing file(s) to the project directory, or update the `src` to point at existing files.

### `duplicate_audio_track`

**Warning.** Two audible elements overlap on the same track index, so their audio doubles up.

**Fix:** Use non-overlapping time windows or different track indices.

### `texture_mask_asset_not_found`

**Error.** A CSS `mask-image` or `-webkit-mask-image` declaration references files that are not in the project, so the texture mask fails to load. In valid CSS, comments and text inside other declarations, such as `content` strings, are ignored.

**Fix:** Add the missing mask file(s) to the project, or update the `mask-image` URL.

### `missing_stylesheet_asset`

**Warning.** A `url()` in a linked local stylesheet does not resolve beside that stylesheet. Browsers resolve `url()` from the stylesheet's own folder, so the font or image 404s and the render falls back silently. When the file exists in a parent folder, the fix hint names the working path.

**Fix:** Change the `url()` to be relative to the stylesheet (for example `../assets/fonts/x.ttf` from `styles/main.css`), or add the file.

### `inaccessible_media_url`
